To prepare teachers and other educators to take a leadership role in the development and implementation of instructional programs for multilingual learners; 2. To prepare researchers in the field of multilingual learner education.

Students complete a combination of coursework and supervised fieldwork to satisfy the requirements for the BCBA® examination. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to work with individuals with a variety of disabilities, including autism, developmental disabilities, and emotional/behavioral disorders. Students learn the concepts and principles of behavior analysis, research methods in behavior analysis, and the application of ABA to a wide range of populations and settings.

Description: The School Psychology program at California State University, Long Beach is a 3-year full-time program that results in an Education Specialist (Ed.S.) degree in School Psychology and a Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) Credential in School Psychology. The program is accredited by the National Association of School Psychologists (NASP) and the Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CTC). The program is designed for students who are committed to working as school psychologists in public schools. The program emphasizes a scientist-practitioner model, which means that students are trained to use research and data to inform their practice as school psychologists. Students in the program take courses in a variety of areas, including assessment, intervention, consultation, law and ethics, and research methods. They also complete several practicum experiences and a year-long internship in a school setting.

Students are also eligible for the Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) Credential in School Psychology. Our program is a trainer-of-trainers (ToT) model for the National Association of School Psychologists (NASP) PREPaRE Curriculum.

Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the College of Global Futures. Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in any field from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in an applicable master's degree program. All applicants must submit: graduate admission application and application fee, official transcripts, personal statement, professional resume, three letters of recommendation, and proof of English proficiency.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Software Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Master of Science in Software Engineering, applicants must have a bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field from a regionally accredited institution, with a minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 semester units (or 90 quarter units). International students must meet the university's English language proficiency requirements. Application materials must include official transcripts, a statement of purpose, and a current resume. GRE scores are currently not required for this program.
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Special Education (Applied Behavior Analysis)
Requirements: Applicants must meet the following requirements for admission to the program: 1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university. 2. A minimum 3.0 overall GPA in the last 60 semester (90 quarter) units of study. 3. Verification of experience (minimum 6 months) working with individuals with disabilities. 4. Two letters of recommendation. 5. A current resume. 6. A statement of purpose.
Description: The Master of Arts in Special Education, Option in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is designed to provide students with advanced knowledge and skills in the principles and practice of behavior analysis. This program is intended for students who are interested in working with individuals with disabilities, including autism spectrum disorders, in a variety of settings such as schools, clinics, and community-based organizations. The coursework in this program is verified by the Association for Behavior Analysis International (ABAI) as meeting the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® (BCBA®) examination. Applicants must meet the requirements for admission to the university and the College of Education. The program emphasizes the application of behavior-analytic principles to improve the lives of individuals with disabilities and their families through evidence-based practices and ethical clinical skills.
Accredidation: Verified Course Sequence (VCS) by the Association for Behavior Analysis International (ABAI); The College of Education at CSULB is accredited by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CTC) and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Sustainable Food Systems
Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the College of Global Futures. Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in any field from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in an applicable master's degree program. All applicants must submit: graduate admission application and application fee, official transcripts, statement of purpose, professional resume, three letters of recommendation, and proof of English proficiency.
Description: The Master of Science in Sustainable Food Systems is a 30-unit interdisciplinary degree that resides within the Department of Family and Consumer Sciences. This program is designed to prepare students for a variety of roles within food-related careers including community food security, agricultural production and research, sustainable food system advocacy, and food policy. Specialized knowledge in community food security, food policy, food system advocacy, and agricultural production/research is gained through core requirements (9 units), focused coursework (12 units), directed research/thesis (3 units), and capstone/electives (6 units).
Accredidation: The Department of Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) is accredited by the American Association of Family and Consumer Sciences (AAFCS).

ProgramName: Master of Public Administration
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Master of Public Administration program, applicants must meet the following requirements: A baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution; A grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter units of study (applicants with a GPA between 2.7 and 2.99 may be considered for 'conditional' admission); Completion of two prerequisite courses: Introduction to American Government and an introductory Statistics course, with a grade of 'C' or better; GRE scores are not required; Three letters of recommendation; A current Resume; and a Statement of Purpose (no more than 500 words).
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Master of Public Administration (MPA) program at CSULB is designed to provide high-quality graduate education for current and future public and nonprofit administrators. Our program is designed to prepare students for leadership roles in the public and nonprofit sectors by providing them with the necessary knowledge and skills to address complex societal problems.
Accredidation: The MPA program is accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA).

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Online MBA program, applicants must meet the following criteria: A bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited university; A minimum GPA of 2.75 in the last 60 semester (90 quarter) units of upper-division and graduate courses; A professional resume; A Video Statement of Purpose; and a Short Answer Personal Statement. Professional work experience is preferred but not required.
Description: The Online MBA (OMBA) program is designed for professionals who want to enhance their management and leadership skills through an entirely online format. The OMBA is a 21-month, 48-unit program. The OMBA is a cohort-based program, which means that students will move through the program with the same group of peers, allowing for networking and collaboration. The program provides the flexibility and convenience of an online education with the quality and prestige of the CSULB College of Business.
Accredidation: AACSB International

ProgramName: Master of Social Work
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. A grade point average of 2.5 or better for the last 60 semester units or 90 quarter units of undergraduate or graduate work is required. Applicants must have a liberal arts background. This background must include at least one course in human biology and one course in elementary statistics with a grade of 'C' or better.
Concentration: Child and Family Wellbeing, Adulthood and Aging, Integrated Health
Description: The Master of Social Work (MSW) program at CSULB is designed to prepare students for advanced professional social work practice. The program provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to work with diverse populations in a variety of settings, including public and private agencies, schools, hospitals, and community-based organizations. Our program offers three specializations: Child and Family Wellbeing, Adulthood and Aging, and Integrated Health. The program's mission is to prepare graduate students to serve as ethical, competent, and effective social work professionals who are committed to social and economic justice and to the enhancement of the well-being of individuals, families, groups, and communities in a diverse society.
Accredidation: The Master of Social Work program at California State University, Long Beach is fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, and specialized program stipends (e.g., CalSWEC Title IV-E Child Welfare Stipend)

ProgramName: Doctor of Nursing Practice
Requirements: Possession of a master's degree in nursing or a related field (e.g., Public Health, Healthcare Administration/Business) from a program accredited by CCNE or ACEN. Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher in the master’s program. Current, active, unencumbered California RN license. National certification in an advanced nursing specialty. Three letters of recommendation. Professional resume or curriculum vitae. Personal statement. Personal interview with the DNP Admission Committee.
Description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) is a terminal degree in nursing that prepares students for the highest level of nursing practice. The DNP degree is a practice-focused doctorate that provides an alternative to research-focused doctoral programs. The DNP program prepares graduates to perform at the highest level of advanced nursing practice, to lead in the clinical setting, and to translate research into clinical practice to improve health outcomes. The DNP program at California State University, Long Beach (CSULB) is a post-master’s program. The program is 5 semesters (2 years) in length. Students are admitted as a cohort in the fall semester of each year. The DNP program focuses on clinical practice, leadership, and research application.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Nursing Practice program at California State University, Long Beach is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org).

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing
Requirements: Admission to the program will be based on the following: 1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution with a major in English or its equivalent. Students with a major in other fields may be admitted at the discretion of the MFA admissions committee provided they have taken at least 24 units of upper-division courses in English (including creative writing and literature). 2. Academic achievement in upper-division English and creative writing courses (at least a 3.0 GPA). 3. Writing portfolio in the applicant’s chosen genre (fiction, poetry, or creative non-fiction). 4. Personal statement of goals and history as a writer. 5. Letters of recommendation from three persons familiar with the applicant’s academic or creative work. 6. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to the MFA in Creative Writing.
Department: College of Liberal Arts, Department of English
Description: The Master of Fine Arts degree in Creative Writing is a 48-unit, professional degree program designed to prepare students for careers in writing and teaching. This program provides professional training in three areas of concentration: fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction. It offers students the opportunity to learn the techniques of their craft, to study the historical and theoretical contexts of their genre, and to produce a book-length work of high literary quality.

ProgramName: Master of Liberal Studies
Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in any field from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in an applicable master's degree program. All applicants must submit: graduate admission application and fee, official transcripts, personal statement, resume, three letters of recommendation, and proof of English proficiency.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Urban and Environmental Planning
Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions. Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in any field from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in an applicable master's degree program. All applicants must submit: graduate admission application and application fee, official transcripts, two letters of recommendation, statement of personal and career goals, professional resume, and proof of English proficiency.
Department: School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning

ProgramName: Master of Legal Studies
Department: Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law
Description: The Certificate in Legal Studies is designed for students who are interested in law-related careers or who are considering law school. The program provides students with a broad-based, interdisciplinary study of the law and legal institutions, and it allows them to explore the role of law in society from various perspectives.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Information Technology
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MSIS program, applicants must have: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution; Minimum 2.75 overall GPA; Submission of the GMAT or GRE (waived for applicants with 3.25 or higher GPA); A current resume; A statement of purpose; Two letters of recommendation.
Description: The Master of Science in Information Systems (MSIS) is a 30-unit program designed to provide students with the advanced knowledge and skills needed to successfully manage and lead in the rapidly changing field of information technology. The program focuses on the strategic use of information systems to improve organizational performance and competitive advantage. Students will learn about the latest trends and technologies in the field, including data analytics, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and social media. They will also develop the leadership and communication skills necessary to effectively manage teams and projects.
Accredidation: The College of Business at CSULB is accredited by AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Engineering (Electrical Engineering)
Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering. Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in engineering, physical sciences, mathematics or a similar field from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in an applicable master's degree program. All applicants must submit: graduate admission application and application fee, official transcripts, statement of purpose, proof of English proficiency (if applicable).
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Concentration: Communications and Digital Signal Processing, Control Systems and Robotics, Electronics and Integrated Circuits, and Power Systems
Description: The Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (MSEE) program at CSULB is designed to provide students with a rigorous foundation in the theoretical and practical aspects of electrical engineering. The program offers students the opportunity to advance their knowledge and skills in specialized areas, preparing them for professional advancement in industry or for further graduate study leading to a doctoral degree. Students can tailor their studies to their career goals through specialization in areas such as Communications and Digital Signal Processing, Control Systems and Robotics, Electronics and Integrated Circuits, and Power Systems.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Engineering (Mechanical Engineering)
Requirements: A bachelor's degree from an accredited program in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a closely related field. A minimum grade point average of 3.0 or higher is required for the last 60 semester units (90 quarter units) of undergraduate work. International applicants must also provide proof of English language proficiency. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission.
Concentration: Thermal, Fluids, and Energy; Solid Mechanics, Materials, and Design; Control, Robotics, and Manufacturing; Modeling, Simulation, and AI
Description: The Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering degree provides students with an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge of mechanical engineering and to specialize in an area of interest. It is designed to prepare students for professional practice in mechanical engineering, for further graduate study at the doctoral level, or for a career in research and development. In addition to the requirements for the degree, which include a core of three courses and five elective courses, the student must either complete a thesis or pass a comprehensive examination. Students must also fulfill the University requirements for graduate degrees.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Communication
Requirements: 1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. 2. A major or minor in communication studies or a related field. 3. An overall grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better. 4. A grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better in their communication studies or related major or minor.
Description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) in Communication Studies is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the field of communication studies, its research methods, and its application to various contexts. The program provides students with the skills and knowledge to pursue a doctoral degree or to pursue a career in a variety of fields, including education, government, and the private sector. Areas of Study include: Interpersonal/Organizational Communication and Rhetoric/Public Address/Social Justice.
ScholarshipType: Departmental Scholarships, Teaching Associates (TAs), Graduate Assistants (GAs)

ProgramName: PhD in Biological Design
Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering. Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in biology, computer science, engineering, geology, mathematics, physical science or a related field from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in an applicable master's degree program. All applicants must submit: 1. graduate admission application and fee 2. official transcripts 3. personal statement 4. resume or curriculum vitae 5. three letters of recommendation 6. proof of English proficiency
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering

ProgramName: PhD in Sustainability
Requirements: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the School of Sustainability. Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree from a regionally accredited institution, in any field. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25 (scale is 4.00 = 'A') in an applicable master's degree program. All applicants must submit: graduate admission application and fee, official transcripts, personal statement, resume or curriculum vitae, three letters of recommendation, writing sample, and proof of English proficiency (if applicable).

ProgramName: PhD in Global Health
Requirements: Applicants must have a Master of Public Health (MPH) degree or an equivalent master’s or doctoral degree in a related field from an accredited institution. Applicants with a master’s degree in another field may be required to complete additional prerequisite coursework in public health. Minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 in the qualifying degree. Standardized graduate entrance exams (e.g., Graduate Record Examination (GRE), Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT), Law School Admission Test (LSAT), or Medical College Admission Test (MCAT)) are optional for admission to the program. Applicants must have at least three years of professional experience in public health or a related field. Evidence of leadership in public health or a related field. Professional writing sample. Three letters of recommendation. A personal statement. Resume or curriculum vitae. Personal interview. International students must meet the university’s English language proficiency requirements (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE).
Department: School of Human Evolution and Social Change
Description: The Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) is a professional, terminal degree designed for individuals seeking leadership roles in public health practice, policy, and advocacy. The program prepares students to address complex public health challenges, lead diverse teams, and implement evidence-based interventions to improve population health outcomes. The concentration in Global Health prepares students to apply their leadership and practice skills in international settings or with diverse global populations in the United States. The curriculum focuses on understanding the global burden of disease, global health systems, and the socio-economic, political, and environmental factors that influence health globally.
Accredidation: Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Forensic Science
Department: New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences
Description: The Master of Science in Forensic Science (MSFS) is a professional degree designed to prepare students for careers in forensic science or for advancement in their current professional careers. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the scientific and technical aspects of forensic science, as well as an understanding of the legal and ethical issues involved in the field. Students will learn about the collection, analysis, and interpretation of physical evidence, and how to communicate their findings in a legal setting.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Criminology and Criminal Justice
Requirements: A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. An upper-division grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 semester (90 quarter) units of study. Applicants must have completed the following prerequisite courses (or their equivalents) with a grade of 'C' or better: Elementary Statistics, Research Methods, and Criminological Theory.
Department: Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions
Description: The Master of Science in Criminology and Criminal Justice is designed to provide a high quality of education for students who wish to pursue a career in any of the many areas of criminal justice or to continue their education at the doctoral level. Through the completion of this program, students will: (1) acquire a sophisticated understanding of the nature and causes of crime and the structure and function of the criminal justice system; (2) develop the research and analytical skills necessary for identifying and solving problems in the field of criminal justice; and (3) enhance their ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in History
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Arts in History requires a minimum 3.0 GPA in upper-division history courses. Applicants must submit a statement of purpose (approximately 500 words), a curriculum vitae or resume, two letters of recommendation, and a writing sample (10-20 pages). The GRE is not required for application to this program.
Department: School of Historical, Philosophical and Religious Studies
Description: The Master of Arts in History provides students with an opportunity to pursue advanced study in history. It is designed to prepare students for teaching at the secondary or community college level, for doctoral study, and for careers in public history, law, business, or government. The program offers training in research, writing, and analytical thinking, focusing on specific geographical areas and time periods while also encouraging comparative and global perspectives.

ProgramName: PhD in English
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Music in Vocal Performance (Opera Emphasis)
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in music or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum grade point average of 3.0 in the last 60 units of study is required for admission to the program. A successful performance audition is required for all performance applicants. Additional materials include three letters of recommendation, a professional resume, and a statement of purpose. All graduate students in the MM program must take placement examinations in music history and music theory. For Vocal Performance specifically, foreign language proficiency in French, German, and Italian is expected.
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts
Description: The Master of Music (M.M.) degree is intended to provide the student with a professional-level competence in the area of specialization. This degree requires a high level of performance or composition and a solid foundation in music history and music theory. The Performance Option is designed to provide students with the opportunity for advanced study in their chosen field of specialization. The program is designed to develop the student’s ability to conduct independent research and to achieve a high level of professional competence in their area of specialization. The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music offers a Master of Music degree in Vocal Performance designed to prepare singers for professional careers in performance and teaching. Students receive intensive training in vocal technique, repertoire, and performance practice, with numerous opportunities to perform in operas, recitals, and ensembles.
Accredidation: The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies
Requirements: Admission as a freshman to CSULB is based on a combination of a student's high school grade point average (GPA) in the 'a-g' subject requirements and other factors. To be considered for admission, applicants must: 1. Graduate from high school by the end of the Spring term prior to Fall enrollment. 2. Complete each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory curriculum (A-G) with a grade of C or better prior to high school graduation.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies degree requires 36 units of Africana Studies courses. Of these, 18 units must be upper division. All students must complete AFRS 100, 110, 215, 319, 498 and 499. For the remaining 18 units, students can take courses in several areas: History, Literature and the Arts, Social Sciences and Cultural Studies. The Africana Studies degree is designed to provide students with a broad and comprehensive understanding of the African World - which includes the Continent of Africa and its Diaspora in the Americas (North, Central and South), the Caribbean and Europe. Students are encouraged to develop their own areas of interest by selecting courses from several areas including history, literature and the arts, social sciences and cultural studies.

ProgramName: Minor in Africana Studies
Requirements: The Minor in Africana Studies consists of 18-19 units. To be eligible for the minor, students must complete the following course requirements: AFRS 110 - Introduction to Africana Studies (3 units) and either AFRS 201 - Design and Social Research in Africana Studies (3 units) or AFRS 215 - U.S. Diversity and the Ethnic Experience (3 units). Additionally, students must complete 12 units of upper division Africana Studies courses, with at least three units from each of the following areas: Area 1: History and Politics, Area 2: Literature and the Arts, and Area 3: Social Science and Psychology.
Description: Africana Studies (AS) is the systematic study of the history, culture, and politics of African-descended people around the world. As an academic discipline, Africana Studies has its roots in the 1960’s Black Studies Movement, which sought to challenge traditional academic narratives and promote a more inclusive and accurate understanding of the Black experience. Our department offers a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree and a Minor in Africana Studies. Our curriculum is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the African Diaspora, from its origins in Africa to its contemporary manifestations in the Americas and beyond. Our courses cover a wide range of topics, including history, literature, music, sociology, political science, and psychology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language Linguistics and Deaf Culture
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the major (for transfer students), applicants must demonstrate a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 and complete required lower-division courses ASL 101 and ASL 102. For the Bachelor of Arts degree, a minimum of 120 units is required, including: Major Requirements (51 units) consisting of ASL 101, 102, 201, 202, and ASLD 101, 124, 211, 212, 305, 306, 324, 401, 411, 412, 424, 434, and 499; General Education Requirements (30-39 units); and Electives (30-39 units).
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in American Sign Language (ASL) Linguistics and Deaf Culture provides students with a strong foundation in the linguistic structure of ASL and an in-depth understanding of the history, culture, and literature of the Deaf community. The program is designed to help students develop high-level proficiency in ASL and gain a critical understanding of the socio-cultural issues that affect the lives of Deaf people. Students will be prepared for a variety of professional careers in fields such as education, social services, advocacy, and linguistics, or for further graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in ASL-English Interpreting
Requirements: To be considered for the Interpreting major, students must complete the following requirements: Completion of ASL 101, 102, 201, and 202 (or the equivalent) with a grade of 'C' or better. Completion of ASL 300 with a grade of 'C' or better. Overall GPA of 3.0 or better. Admission to the major is pending a screening process which includes a screening application form, unofficial transcripts, personal statement, and video sample.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in ASL-English Interpreting (ASLEI) provides students with a comprehensive foundation in the skills and knowledge required to become professional interpreters between American Sign Language (ASL) and English. The program focuses on language development, cultural knowledge, and the cognitive and ethical processes involved in interpreting. Our mission is to prepare students to work as competent and ethical interpreters in a variety of settings, and to provide them with the knowledge and skills they need to pursue national certification.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The ASL-English Interpreting program at CSULB is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Interpreter Education (CCIE).

ProgramName: Minor in American Sign Language Linguistics and Deaf Culture
Requirements: The Minor in American Sign Language Linguistics and Deaf Culture is open to any student. Completion of the minor requires 18-21 units. All courses must be completed with a grade of 'C' or better. To declare the Minor, please contact the Linguistics Department Undergraduate Advisor.
Description: The ASL Linguistics and Deaf Culture Minor is designed to provide students with the ability to communicate in ASL and a solid foundation in the linguistic structure of ASL and the culture and history of the Deaf community.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the American Studies BA, freshman applicants must meet the minimum CSU requirements: high school graduation, completion of the 15-unit 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects with a grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA. Transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0, and have completed the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better. There are no additional lower-division major preparation courses required for admission into this specific major.
Description: American Studies is an interdisciplinary field that examines the history and culture of the United States. Our program encourages students to investigate the complex interactions between social, political, and cultural movements and the ways in which they have shaped American identity. Students explore the diverse experiences of people in the United States and the impact of those experiences on the nation's past and present.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in American Studies
Requirements: A minimum of 18 units, of which at least 12 must be upper division, is required. Students must take the following courses: AMST 300 - Introduction to American Studies (3 units); AMST 350 - California and the West (3 units) or AMST 351 - Celebrity in American Culture (3 units); AMST 498 - Senior Seminar in American Studies (3 units). An additional 9 units of upper division courses chosen from the list of American Studies courses or American Studies related courses in other departments (consult with the Program Director).
Description: American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws from many academic fields to study the diverse cultures of the United States. Its focus is on the American experience, both in its national and international contexts. American Studies students examine the ways in which Americans have thought about themselves and their society, and the ways in which others have viewed them. Through a variety of courses, students explore the historical, literary, artistic, social, and political dimensions of American life.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to CSULB as a freshman, you must graduate from high school, complete the 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects with a grade of C or better, and meet the Multi-Factor Admission Score. Transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, have a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher, and have completed the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning). For the Anthropology BA, transfer applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0.
Description: Anthropology is the study of the biological and cultural origins and development of the human species. It includes the study of human biological variation, the analysis of the archaeological remains of past cultures, and the description and analysis of the diverse cultures of the modern world. The Department of Anthropology is committed to providing students with a high-quality education in the four fields of anthropology: archaeology, biological anthropology, linguistic anthropology, and sociocultural anthropology. The program is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the human experience and to prepare them for a variety of careers in the private and public sectors, as well as for graduate study in anthropology and related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Requirements: A minimum of 18 units in anthropology, including: ANTH 110 - Introduction to Biological Anthropology (3 units), ANTH 120 - Introduction to Cultural Anthropology (3 units), ANTH 150 - Introduction to Archaeology (3 units). In addition, 9 units of upper division anthropology are required. At least 6 of these upper division units must be taken in residence at CSULB.
Description: An Anthropology minor is a great way to explore the diversity of the human experience while adding a global perspective to any major. The minor allows students to sample from the various subfields of the discipline (archaeology, biological, linguistic, and cultural anthropology), or focus on an area of interest.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian and Asian American Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Asian and Asian American Studies, applicants must meet the general California State University (CSU) undergraduate admission requirements. First-time freshmen must have graduated from high school, completed the 'a-g' college preparatory curriculum with a grade of C- or better, and meet the minimum Eligibility Index. Transfer students must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, including the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better, and meet the minimum GPA required for the major.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Asian and Asian American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the histories, cultures, and experiences of people of Asian descent in the United States and globally. The program offers two options: Asian American Studies and Asian Studies. Our curriculum is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the diverse experiences of Asian and Asian American people through a range of disciplines, including history, literature, sociology, political science, and the arts.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies
Requirements: Lower Division Requirements for all concentrations (3 units): ASIA 100 - Introduction to Asian Studies (3 units). Students must also complete 6 units of Lower Division ASAM Courses (options include ASAM 100, 120, 121, 160, 200, 210) and 6 units of Language Courses in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean.
Concentration: Chinese Studies, Japanese Studies, and Korean Studies
Description: The Asian Studies program provides students with an opportunity to gain an understanding of the diverse cultures, histories, and languages of Asia. The major is designed to be interdisciplinary, allowing students to take courses in several different departments. The program offers a Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies and a minor in Asian Studies, with concentrations in Chinese Studies, Japanese Studies, and Korean Studies. Students in the Asian Studies program develop a broad understanding of the Asian continent while gaining specialized knowledge in a particular language and culture.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Departmental (e.g., San-Genshu Scholarship, Japanese Language Scholarship)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian American Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Asian American Studies, applicants must meet the general university admission requirements for California State University, Long Beach. Freshman applicants must have graduated from high school, completed the comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects with a grade of C or better, and meet the eligibility index. Transfer applicants must have completed 60 transferable semester units, including the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C or better, and meet the minimum GPA requirements for the major.
Description: Asian American Studies is an interdisciplinary field of study that focuses on the history, culture, and contemporary experiences of persons of Asian and Pacific Islander ancestry in the United States. The program offers a Bachelor of Arts degree and a minor. The curriculum provides students with a broad understanding of the social, political, and economic factors that have shaped the lives of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, as well as the cultural and artistic expressions of these communities. Students will develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills that will prepare them for a variety of careers and further study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the university as a freshman, applicants must: be a high school graduate or equivalent; complete the 15-unit comprehensive “a-g” pattern of college preparatory study; and earn a qualifying “Admission Index.” Transfer students must have completed 60 or more transferable semester units (90 quarter units) by the end of the prior spring term for fall admission, have a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher in all transferable college coursework, be in good standing at the last college or university attended, and have completed at least 30 units of CSU General Education Breadth with a grade of C- or better.
Description: The Chinese Studies Program offers a Bachelor of Arts in Chinese Studies and a minor in Chinese. The program provides a solid foundation in the Chinese language (Mandarin) and a broad knowledge of Chinese culture, history, and literature. The Chinese Studies Program also offers courses in Chinese calligraphy, film, linguistics, and philosophy. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of Chinese language, literature, culture, and history.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese Studies
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Arts in Japanese Studies, students must complete 33-35 units of upper-division courses. Requirements include lower-division prerequisites JAPN 101, 102, 201, and 202 (or equivalent). Students must also satisfy the university’s general education requirements and other graduation requirements for a total of 120 units. Admission is subject to general university undergraduate admission criteria.
Description: The Japanese program at CSULB is one of the largest and most established Japanese programs in the country. Our curriculum is designed to provide students with a well-rounded education in Japanese language, literature, culture, and linguistics. We offer a wide range of courses, from beginning to advanced levels, as well as courses on Japanese literature, film, pop culture, and society. Our mission is to help students achieve high levels of proficiency in all four language skills (speaking, listening, reading, and writing) and to provide them with a deep understanding of Japanese society and culture. Our faculty are dedicated to providing students with a high-quality education and help them achieve their goals, whether they are interested in pursuing a career in Japan, working in an international environment, or continuing their studies at the graduate level.

ProgramName: Minor in Asian and Asian American Studies
Requirements: The Minor in Asian and Asian American Studies requires 18 units of Asian and Asian American Studies courses, of which 9 units must be upper-division. All courses must be completed with a grade of 'C' or better.
Description: Asian and Asian American Studies (AAAS) is an interdisciplinary program that explores the history, culture, and experiences of people of Asian descent in the United States and globally. The program offers a major and minor that provide students with a solid foundation in the field and prepare them for a variety of careers in fields such as education, law, social work, and business. Students in the program have the opportunity to take courses in a wide range of disciplines, including history, literature, sociology, and political science. They also have the opportunity to participate in internships and research projects that allow them to apply their knowledge in real-world settings.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, community service, and endowed scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chicano and Latino Studies
Requirements: To qualify for the Bachelor of Arts in Chicano and Latino Studies, a student must complete a minimum of 120 units. Students must complete 36 units of Chicano and Latino Studies courses, of which 24 units must be upper division. Requirements for the Major include Lower Division: CHLS 100, CHLS 101, CHLS 200, CHLS 258; and Upper Division: CHLS 300, CHLS 310, CHLS 340, CHLS 350, CHLS 490.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Chicano and Latino Studies is an interdisciplinary major that provides students with a strong foundation in the history, culture, and social issues facing Chicano and Latino communities in the United States. Through a combination of coursework and community-based learning, students gain a deep understanding of the diverse experiences and contributions of Chicanos and Latinos to American society. Graduates of the program are prepared for a variety of careers in fields such as education, social work, public policy, law, and business, as well as for graduate study in a range of disciplines.

ProgramName: Minor in Chicano and Latino Studies
Requirements: The minor in Chicano and Latino Studies requires a minimum of 18 units. Requirements include 6 units of lower-division courses (CHLS 100 and CHLS 101) and 12 units of upper-division courses. All courses for the minor must be taken for a letter grade.
Description: The minor in Chicano and Latino Studies is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the history, culture, and social conditions of people of Mexican and Latin American descent in the United States. The minor is an excellent complement to any major and provides students with the skills and knowledge to work effectively in a diverse and multicultural society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classics
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Classics, applicants must meet the general California State University, Long Beach undergraduate admission criteria. For freshmen, this includes high school graduation, completion of the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects with a grade of C- or better by the end of the spring term prior to fall enrollment. CSULB is a test-blind campus; SAT and ACT scores are not used for admission purposes. For transfer applicants, requirements include completion of 60 transferable semester units (90 quarter units), a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0, and completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better.
Concentration: Greek and Roman Civilization; Latin and Greek Language and Literature; Latin Language and Literature
Description: The Department of Classics offers a variety of courses and programs that examine the civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome. These include the languages (ancient Greek and Latin), the literature, and the history, art, and philosophy of the classical world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ancient Greek
Requirements: Complete a minimum of 31 units in Classics including: RGR 100, CLSC 101, CLSC 202, CLSC 405; A minimum of 15 units of Upper Division Classical Greek; Electives: 6 units of CLSC courses. Major courses must be completed with a C or better.
Description: The Option in Ancient Greek is designed to provide students with a strong command of the ancient Greek language and a broad understanding of ancient Greek literature, history, and culture. The Classics Department offers the B.A. degree in Classics with an option in either Ancient Greek, Latin, or Classical Studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Latin
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Latin program, students must meet the general undergraduate admission requirements for California State University, Long Beach. Freshman applicants must: graduate from high school; complete the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C- or better; and meet the minimum CSU eligibility index. Transfer applicants must: have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units; have a minimum GPA of 2.0 or higher in all transferable college coursework; and have completed at least 30 units of General Education courses with a grade of C- or better, including the 'Golden Four' GE requirements.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Latin provides students with a high level of proficiency in the Latin language and its literature, as well as a broad understanding of the culture and history of ancient Rome and its influence on the Western world. The major consists of 30 units of upper-division courses in Latin and Classics. Of these, 18 units must be in Latin (including LAT 301 and LAT 401), and 12 units may be in Latin, Greek, or Classics (including CLAS 491).
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies, applicants must meet the general California State University, Long Beach undergraduate admission requirements. First-time freshmen must have graduated from high school, completed the 'a-g' college preparatory curriculum with a grade of C or better, and meet the minimum CSU eligibility index. Transfer students must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, including the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better, and maintain a minimum GPA as required by the university.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies is an interdisciplinary major that allows students to study the ancient Greek and Roman worlds through various perspectives including literature, history, art history, philosophy, and archaeology. Unlike the B.A. in Classics, which requires intensive study of Greek or Latin, the B.A. in Classical Studies emphasizes the study of these civilizations through texts in translation and a wide range of elective courses.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Classics
Requirements: The Minor in Classics is available to any student except those majoring in Classics. A student must complete 18 units of Classics courses, of which 9 must be upper division. Students must maintain a minimum GPA of 2.0 in all courses required for the minor.
Description: This minor is designed to provide students with a general knowledge of the civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome and their impact on the modern world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the major, applicants must demonstrate the following: Minimum Cumulative GPA: 2.5; Minimum Lower Division Preparation (grade of C or better required): COMM 110 (Interpersonal Communication), COMM 130 (Essentials of Public Speaking), and COMM 131 (Essentials of Argumentation). Additionally, transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units (90 quarter units) with a grade point average of 2.0 or better by the end of the prior spring term for fall admission, including the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements.
Description: Communication Studies is a multifaceted discipline that explores how people use messages to generate meanings within and across various contexts. It is the discipline that studies all forms, modes, media, and consequences of communication through humanistic, social scientific, and aesthetic inquiry. The Department of Communication Studies provides a curriculum that focuses on the study of communication in various contexts including interpersonal, organizational, intercultural, political, and rhetorical. The Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in communication theory and research, helping them develop the ability to think critically and communicate effectively in diverse social and professional environments.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication Culture and Public Affairs
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to CSULB, undergraduate applicants must meet the following minimum requirements: 1. Graduation from high school or equivalent. 2. Completion of the 15-unit comprehensive 'A-G' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C- or better. 3. Meet the minimum CSU GPA requirement of 2.50 or greater for California residents (3.00 or greater for non-residents). CSULB is 'test-blind' for SAT/ACT scores, meaning they are not used for admission purposes. For Graduate applicants, the minimum requirement is a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 2.5 in the last 60 semester units attempted.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Communication Culture and Public Affairs is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the study of communication as it relates to culture and public life. The program emphasizes the role of communication in shaping social identities, public discourse, and civic engagement. Students learn to analyze and produce messages across various contexts, including interpersonal, organizational, intercultural, and political communication.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interpersonal and Organizational Communication
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Interpersonal and Organizational Communication is based on major-specific requirements. For transfer students, applicants must complete the following major-specific requirements with a grade of 'C' or better: COMM 110 (or 110H), COMM 130, and COMM 131 (or 131H), and have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.50. For first-time freshmen, admission is based on the CSU multi-factor admission criteria, including high school GPA and completion of the 'a-g' college preparatory curriculum with a grade of C- or better.
Description: The Interpersonal and Organizational Communication (IOC) area of study focuses on the ways in which people communicate in their personal and professional lives. Research and teaching in this area examine communication in a variety of contexts, including families, friendships, romantic relationships, and workplaces. Our faculty members investigate how people manage conflict, provide social support, influence others, and build and maintain relationships. We also examine how communication shapes organizational culture, leadership, and decision-making.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Communication Studies
Requirements: This minor is available to any student who is not a Communication Studies major. Students must have a 2.5 overall GPA to declare the minor. A minimum of 21 units in Communication Studies is required, including: COMM 110; COMM 306; and either COMM 334 or COMM 335. Additionally, 12 units of Communication Studies elective courses are required, 9 of which must be upper-division.
Description: The minor in Communication Studies is designed to provide students with a general background in the field of communication studies. Students may select courses that best meet their educational and professional needs.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative World Literature
Requirements: Admission to all majors at CSULB is competitive. Freshman applicants must meet the following minimum requirements: 1. Graduate from high school or have a GED; 2. Complete the 'A-G' 15-unit comprehensive pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C- or better by the end of high school; 3. Meet the minimum GPA requirement for the major. Transfer applicants must: 1. Complete a minimum of 60 transferable semester units; 2. Complete the 'Golden Four' GE courses with a grade of C or better; 3. Meet the major-specific GPA and required lower-division preparation.
Description: The Department of Comparative World Literature and Classics offers an undergraduate major and minor in Comparative World Literature. The Comparative World Literature program provides students with an opportunity to study world literature and culture from an interdisciplinary and international perspective. The curriculum focuses on the study of literary texts in their cultural and historical contexts, and on the relationships between literature and other fields of inquiry, such as philosophy, the arts, and the social sciences. Students in the program develop skills in critical analysis, research, and communication, and gain a broad understanding of the world's diverse literary and cultural traditions. Our program offers students the opportunity to explore the diverse ways in which humans have expressed their experiences and ideas through literature, film, and other media. Students will learn to analyze texts from a variety of historical periods and cultural traditions, and will develop the skills in critical thinking, writing, and research that are necessary for success in a globalized world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Comparative World Literature
Requirements: The minor in Comparative World Literature consists of 18 units, of which 12 units must be upper division. Required courses include: CWL 100 - Introduction to World Literature (3 units), CWL 210 - Eroticism, Love, and Sensuality (3 units), and 12 units of upper-division Comparative World Literature (CWL) courses.
Description: Comparative World Literature (CWL) involves the study of literature and culture across national, linguistic, and disciplinary boundaries. CWL students are passionate about reading and thinking about books and films from around the world. Because our field is comparative, we look for connections and intersections between literatures, and between literature and other fields of study (such as film, the visual arts, psychology, philosophy, and history).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Economics, applicants must meet the general university admission requirements. For freshmen, this includes completion of the A-G college preparatory sequence. Transfer students must complete a minimum of 60 transferable units, including the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements and specific major preparation courses: ECON 100 (Principles of Microeconomics), ECON 101 (Principles of Macroeconomics), and one of the following math courses: MATH 115, MATH 119A, or MATH 122. All major preparation courses must be completed with a grade of 'C' or better.
Description: The study of economics provides an understanding of how our economic system works and how economic decisions are made by individuals, businesses, and governments. Economics is a versatile degree that prepares students for a variety of careers in business, government, and non-profit organizations, as well as for graduate study in economics, business, law, and public policy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematical Economics
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Mathematical Economics, applicants must meet the general California State University (CSU) undergraduate admission requirements. Transfer applicants must complete specific major-specific requirements with a grade of 'C' or better, including: ECON 100 (Principles of Macroeconomics), ECON 101 (Principles of Microeconomics), MATH 122 (Calculus I), and MATH 123 (Calculus II). A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 is required for transfer students.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Mathematical Economics is a joint program offered by the Department of Economics and the Department of Mathematics and Statistics. It is designed for students who intend to pursue graduate study in economics or for those who desire more of a mathematical focus in their undergraduate training. This program is also helpful for students who are planning to pursue a more technical MBA. Students who intend to pursue a Ph.D. in economics are especially encouraged to consider this major. Students may choose between the Department of Economics and the Department of Mathematics and Statistics for their major advising. However, all students in this program are encouraged to see the Mathematical Economics advisor in the Department of Economics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economic Theory
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Economic Theory, applicants must meet general university admission requirements. For first-year students, this includes high school graduation and completion of the 'A-G' college preparatory subjects with a qualifying GPA. For transfer students, admission requires the completion of major preparation courses including ECON 100 (Principles of Microeconomics), ECON 101 (Principles of Macroeconomics), and MATH 115 or MATH 122 with a grade of 'C' or better. The program requires a total of 120 units, including core courses such as ECON 310, ECON 311, ECON 410, ECON 411, ECON 420, and mathematics courses including MATH 122, MATH 123, MATH 224, and MATH 247.
Description: This option is intended for students who wish to prepare for graduate study in economics. It requires a stronger foundation in mathematics and more rigorous study of economic theory than the regular Bachelor of Arts degree.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Economics
Requirements: The minor in Economics is available to any non-Economics major. To declare the minor, students must have a minimum 2.0 GPA in the three prerequisite courses: ECON 100, ECON 101, and MATH 115 (or MATH 119A or MATH 122). The minor requires a minimum of 21 units in Economics, of which at least 15 units must be upper-division. All courses for the minor must be taken for a letter grade.
Description: The Minor in Economics is designed for students who want to develop a basic understanding of economic principles and their application to a variety of social and business problems. This minor is open to all students except those majoring in Economics, Mathematical Economics and Economic Theory, or Business Economics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in English is based on the applicant's reported GPA and completion of the 'a-g' college preparatory subjects for freshman applicants. Transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics), and specific major-specific preparation including ENGL 180 (Introduction to Literature) with a minimum GPA of 2.5.
Concentration: Creative Writing, English Education, Literature, Rhetoric and Composition
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in English provides students with a broad knowledge of literature written in English and of the history and structure of the English language. It also helps students develop the ability to read and write with critical and creative insight. Students are expected to demonstrate knowledge of the works of major writers, of the development of the various literary genres, and of the basic principles of literary criticism. They are also expected to develop a high level of proficiency in writing.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Literature
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to CSULB as a freshman, you must: complete each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory subjects (A-G) with a grade of C or higher; and graduate from high school.
Description: The Literature option provides a comprehensive foundation in British, American, and World literature in English. It prepares students for graduate study in English, comparative literature, and other humanistic disciplines, as well as for careers in teaching, law, publishing, and business. In addition to a core of six literature courses, students in this option take seven upper-division electives in literature and a senior seminar.
Accredidation: California State University, Long Beach is accredited by the WASC Senior College and University Commission (WSCUC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Creative Writing
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in English, Option in Creative Writing is based on general university undergraduate admission criteria. Freshman applicants must have graduated from high school, completed the 'a-g' college preparatory course sequence with a grade of C- or better, and meet the CSU Multi-Factor Admission Criteria. Transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, maintained a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher, be in good standing at the last college or university attended, and have completed the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better.
Description: The Creative Writing program at CSULB is one of the oldest and most prestigious in the country. Our faculty consists of award-winning poets and fiction writers who are dedicated to helping students find and develop their own creative voices. We offer a Bachelor of Arts in English with an option in Creative Writing, as well as a Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing. Our curriculum includes workshops in poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction, as well as courses in literature and form and theory.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Rhetoric and Composition
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in English, Option in Rhetoric and Composition follows the general undergraduate admission requirements for California State University, Long Beach. For first-time freshmen, eligibility is based on a multi-factor admission process that includes the completion of the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects with grades of C- or better and the high school GPA. For transfer students, requirements include the completion of 60 transferable semester units, a minimum GPA of 2.0 or higher in all transferable college coursework, and the completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better. The Department of English does not require additional supplemental materials for this program.
Description: The Rhetoric and Composition Option is designed for students who are interested in the study of language, writing, and the history and theory of rhetoric. Students in this option explore how discourse shaped historical movements and continues to shape contemporary culture. The program provides a foundation for careers in teaching, law, public relations, professional writing, and advanced study in rhetoric and composition.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English Education
Requirements: Students must take the following courses to fulfill the Option in English Education: English 300, English 310, English 320, English 363, and English 404. In addition, students are required to take courses in the following areas: Literature Survey Requirements (6 units), English Education Breadth and Depth (6 units), English Language and Composition (6 units), and Extended Studies (12 units). English Education students must maintain a 3.0 or higher in all English coursework.
Description: The Option in English Education provides students with the subject matter preparation required by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing for the Single Subject Teaching Credential in English. This program is for students who want to become middle school or high school English teachers.
Accredidation: Approved by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC) for the Single Subject Teaching Credential in English

ProgramName: Minor in English
Requirements: A minor in English is available to any student majoring in another field. To declare the minor, students must meet with a department advisor. The minor consists of 18-21 units, and a grade of 'C' or better is required in all courses used to satisfy the requirements for the minor.
Description: The Minor in English is available to any non-English major. It allows students to supplement their major with an abbreviated program of study in literature and/or creative writing. Students might choose to minor in English for personal enrichment or to develop the writing and analytical skills that will facilitate their career goals. The program requires 18 units, at least 12 of which must be upper-division.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Science and Policy
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Science and Policy is offered through the College of Liberal Arts and the College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics. REQUIREMENTS: Lower Division: Take all the following: BIOL 153 or 211; CHEM 100 or 111A; ECON 201; GEOG 130 or 140; GEOL 102; ESP 200. Upper Division: Take all the following: ESP 400; GEOG 481; PHIL 403 or 489; POSC 311; ECON 462. A minimum of 18 units of electives is required.
Description: This interdisciplinary degree program provides students with the necessary knowledge and skills for a career in environmental management, environmental law, environmental education, or the pursuit of graduate studies in related fields. The program emphasizes the integration of physical and biological sciences with social sciences and humanities to address environmental challenges.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science and Policy
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the B.S. in Environmental Science and Policy, transfer applicants must demonstrate the following: a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and completion of specific lower-division preparation courses, including BIOL 211, CHEM 111A, MATH 119A or MATH 122, and one of the following: GEOG 140 or GEOL 102 and GEOL 104 with a grade of 'C' or better. For first-time freshmen, CSULB is an impacted campus and admission is based on the CSU eligibility index (GPA and 'a-g' requirements); SAT and ACT scores are not used for admission purposes.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Environmental Science and Policy (ES&P) program is an interdisciplinary program that leads to either a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) or a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree. The ES&P program at CSULB is a unique collaboration between the College of Liberal Arts and the College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics. It provides students with the interdisciplinary training necessary to understand and solve complex environmental problems. Students gain a strong foundation in the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities, and they learn how to apply this knowledge to real-world environmental issues.

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Science and Policy
Requirements: This minor is available to any student who has completed GE Foundation requirements, has a minimum 2.0 GPA in all work completed, and has been admitted to a major. Students must complete a minimum of 21-22 units.
Description: The Environmental Science and Policy (ES&P) program is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with a foundational understanding of the environment and the role that humans play in it. The program is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge needed to address environmental issues from a variety of perspectives, including science, policy, and ethics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
CostPerCredit: $396 per unit (for non-residents, in addition to mandatory fees)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French and Francophone Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the French and Francophone Studies major, an individual must be eligible for admission to the University. For freshmen, admission is based on the CSU eligibility index which considers high school GPA and completion of the A-G college preparatory subjects. For transfer students, requirements include the completion of 60 transferable semester units, a minimum GPA of 2.0 or higher in all transferable college coursework, and completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C or better.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in French and Francophone Studies provides students with a solid foundation in the French language and the literatures and cultures of the French-speaking world. The program is designed to help students develop a high level of proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing French, and to provide them with a broad knowledge of French and Francophone literature, culture, and civilization. The program also aims to develop students’ analytical and critical thinking skills and to prepare them for a variety of careers or for further study at the graduate level.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in French and Francophone Studies
Requirements: 18 units of which 12 must be upper division. Prerequisites: Completion of FREN 101B or 102 or equivalent.
Description: The French and Francophone Studies program at CSULB is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the French language and the diverse cultures of the French-speaking world.
