Our curriculum focuses on developing linguistic proficiency, critical thinking skills, and cultural awareness through the study of literature, film, history, and contemporary society. Students in our program have the opportunity to engage with faculty who are experts in their fields and to participate in study abroad programs that offer immersive language and cultural experiences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Geography is based on the general California State University, Long Beach undergraduate admission requirements. Freshmen applicants must meet the following criteria: 1. Complete each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory subjects (A-G) with a grade of C or better. 2. Be a high school graduate or have a GED. 3. Meet the Multi-Factor Admission Criteria (MFAC) which considers high school GPA and other factors. Transfer applicants must have completed 60 transferable semester units, the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a C- or better, and required lower-division major preparation.
Description: Geography is a spatial science that studies the location and distribution of phenomena on the Earth’s surface. It investigates the ways in which people and their environments interact and how these interactions lead to the creation of unique places and regions. Geography uses an integrated approach to analyze world issues like climate change, sustainability, social and economic inequality, urban development, and global health. Students learn to use spatial analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and field methods to help solve real-world problems.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
CostPerCredit: $420/unit (Non-resident fee in addition to mandatory tuition)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geography
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Geography, applicants must meet general California State University (CSU) admission requirements. Freshmen must complete the 'A-G' college preparatory sequence with a grade of C or better and meet the competitive eligibility index. Transfer students must have a minimum of 60 transferable units, a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0, and have completed specific major-specific preparation with a grade of C or better, which includes GEOG 100 - World Regional Geography and either GEOG 130 - Geography of Weather and Climate or GEOG 140 - Introduction to Physical Geography.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Geography is designed for students seeking a more technical and science-oriented program of study. It requires more coursework in mathematics and science than the Bachelor of Arts in Geography, and provides a strong foundation in physical geography and geospatial techniques. Students in the B.S. program often go on to careers in environmental consulting, natural resource management, urban and regional planning, and geospatial technology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Geography
Requirements: A minimum of 18 units in Geography, of which at least 9 must be upper division. Required Courses include: GEOG 100 - World Regional Geography (3 units); GEOG 110 - Physical Geography (3 units) OR GEOG 140 - Introduction to Physical Geography (3 units); GEOG 160 - Introduction to Human Geography (3 units). In addition, 9 units of electives are required, all of which must be upper division.
Description: Geography is the study of the Earth’s surface, including the distribution of its physical and cultural features. It is a unique discipline that bridges the natural and social sciences. Geographers analyze the spatial relationships between people, places, and the environment. They use a variety of tools, including Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and field observations, to understand and address complex global issues such as climate change, urban development, and resource management. The minor in geography is an excellent complement to many majors across the university. Students learn about the world’s people, places, and environments, and develop skills in spatial analysis and geographic technologies.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to CSULB as a freshman, you must: complete each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory 'a-g' subjects with a grade of C or better prior to high school graduation; and meet a minimum Multi-Factor Admission Score (MFAS) based on high school GPA. For the Bachelor of Arts in German, students must complete a minimum of 120 units, including specific lower-division courses (GERM 101A, 101B, 201A, 201B) or their equivalents, and 30 units of upper-division courses with a minimum GPA of 2.0.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in German provides a foundation for the study of German language, literature and culture. It is designed for students who wish to pursue a variety of career goals, including teaching, international business, translation and interpretation, and positions in government and industry. It also provides preparation for graduate study in German.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in German
Requirements: A minor in German consists of a minimum of 18 units of German courses, of which 6 units must be upper division. Lower Division: Take all of the following: GERM 101A - Fundamentals of German (4 units), GERM 101B - Fundamentals of German (4 units), GERM 201A - Intermediate German (4 units), GERM 201B - Intermediate German (4 units). Upper Division: Take 6 units of upper-division courses in German.
Description: The minor in German is available to students in any major. It is designed to provide students with a functional proficiency in the German language and a broad knowledge of German literature and culture.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies is based on the university's general undergraduate admission criteria. For first-time freshmen, this includes high school graduation, completion of the 'a-g' college preparatory subjects, and meeting the Multi-Factor Admission Criteria (MFAC) which primarily considers high school GPA. For transfer students, requirements include the completion of 60 transferable units by the end of the prior spring term for fall admission, a minimum cumulative GPA (typically 2.5 or higher for this major), being in good standing at the last college attended, and completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C or better.
Description: The Global Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that offers students the opportunity to study the world’s regions and the interactions among them from a variety of perspectives. The program provides students with a broad understanding of global issues and the skills to analyze and address them. The curriculum focuses on the study of the history, politics, economics, and culture of different regions of the world, as well as the ways in which these regions are connected through globalization. Students learn to think critically about global issues such as climate change, human rights, international development, and global health, and to develop solutions to these challenges.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in History program is based on CSULB's general undergraduate admission criteria. For first-time freshmen, eligibility is determined by a combination of high school GPA and completion of the 'a-g' college preparatory subjects. For transfer applicants, the History major is impacted. Transfer students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 and must have completed the following major preparation courses with a grade of 'C' or better: HIST 172 (Early Modern World History) and HIST 173 (Modern World History). Additionally, transfers must have completed the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning).
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in History is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the human past, from ancient times to the present, and from a global perspective. Our program emphasizes critical thinking, research skills, and clear communication, preparing students for a wide range of careers and for further study in history, law, education, and other fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in History
Requirements: A minimum of 18 units in history, of which 9 units must be upper division. All history courses in the minor must be taken for a letter grade. To be eligible for the History minor, students must have a minimum GPA of 2.0 in the History courses already completed.
Description: This minor is available to any student who is not a History major. The Minor in History is designed for students who want to explore history as a field of study and to develop their research and writing skills. The minor is a flexible program that allows students to choose from a wide range of courses in various geographical areas and time periods. It is designed to complement a student’s major and to provide a broader context for their studies, providing a foundation in historical methods and offering students the opportunity to explore a variety of historical periods and regions.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Human Development
Requirements: Human Development is an impacted major. To be admitted to the major, you must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5. Admission is based on university-wide criteria including the completion of general education requirements and major-specific prerequisites such as HDEV 180, ANTH 120, PSY 100, and SOC 100.
Description: Human Development is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the processes of human growth and development throughout the lifespan. The program integrates research and theory from several different fields including biology, psychology, sociology, and anthropology. This interdisciplinary approach provides students with a broad perspective for understanding how people grow and change, as well as the role of social and cultural contexts in those processes.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the International Studies major, first-time freshmen must have graduated from high school, completed the 15-unit 'A-G' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C- or better, and meet a minimum 'A-G' GPA of 2.5. Transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.50, and have completed the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C or better.
Description: The International Studies (IST) major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of global issues, processes, and systems. It provides students with a broad understanding of the world’s cultures, histories, economies, and political systems, and helps them develop the analytical skills and knowledge needed to address complex international problems. The IST program at CSULB offers a diverse and rigorous curriculum that covers a wide range of topics, including international relations, global development, human rights, environmental sustainability, and cultural studies.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in International Studies
Requirements: The Minor in International Studies is available to all students except those majoring in International Studies. The minor requires a minimum of 21 units. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in all courses for the minor. To declare a minor in International Studies, students must meet with an IST advisor.
Description: The Minor in International Studies offers students an opportunity to take an interdisciplinary approach to global affairs. It provides students with a broad context for their major field of study, while developing their understanding of international politics, economics, and cultures.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Italian Studies
Requirements: The Italian Studies program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in Italian language, culture, and literature. To be a major in Italian Studies, students must have a minimum GPA of 2.0 in the major. General education requirements must also be met. Students who wish to major in Italian Studies must complete 33 units, including 3 units from Italian culture in English and 30 units from Italian culture, literature, and linguistics taught in Italian.
Description: The B.A. in Italian Studies provides students with the linguistic and cultural tools to enter a variety of professions in which knowledge of Italy is required. The program offers a broad-based curriculum that includes language, literature, film, history, and art history. Our students are encouraged to participate in study abroad programs in Italy to further enhance their linguistic skills and cultural understanding. The George L. Graziadio Center for Italian Studies at California State University, Long Beach, is home to one of the largest and most vibrant Italian programs in the United States.

ProgramName: Minor in Italian Studies
Requirements: A minor in Italian Studies consists of 18 units, of which 12 units must be upper division. No more than 6 units of 'Italian Studies' (taught in English) can be applied to the minor. ITAL 101A does not count toward the minor. Students must have a 2.0 GPA in all work completed at CSULB and be in good academic standing. All students must meet with the Italian advisor to plan their minor program.
Description: Italian Studies is an interdisciplinary program that includes the study of Italian language, literature, culture, history, art, and cinema. It is designed to complement a variety of majors by offering students the opportunity to develop linguistic proficiency and cultural competence in Italian, which is essential for careers in international business, diplomacy, education, fashion, and the arts.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Journalism program is based on general California State University (CSU) undergraduate requirements. First-time freshmen must have graduated from high school and completed the 'a-g' college preparatory course pattern with a grade of C or better. For transfer students, the program requires a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C or better, and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0. Additionally, transfer applicants must complete the major-specific prerequisite JOUR 120 (Introduction to Mass Communication) with a grade of C or better.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism provides students with a solid foundation in the concepts and practices of journalism. Students learn to gather, process, and disseminate news and information through various media, including print, broadcast, and digital platforms. The program emphasizes the importance of accuracy, ethics, and the role of a free press in a democratic society. The journalism major is designed to provide students with a strong background in writing, reporting and editing for all media—print, broadcast and online. The program also offers courses in media law, ethics, and history. Students are encouraged to develop their skills through internships and work on student media.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: Accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC)

ProgramName: Minor in Journalism
Requirements: A minimum of 18 units in journalism is required. Requirements include: JOUR 120, JOUR 240, JOUR 300 or JOUR 312, and 9 additional units of upper-division journalism courses. Students must maintain a GPA of 2.0 or higher in all courses required for the minor.
Description: The Journalism minor is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge of the journalism profession and its role in society. Students will learn core skills in reporting, writing and editing, and they will explore the legal and ethical issues that journalists face. It is useful for students in a variety of majors, including those who may want to pursue careers in areas related to journalism.
Accredidation: Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics, applicants must meet the general university admission requirements for California State University, Long Beach. For freshman applicants, this includes graduation from high school, completion of the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects with a grade of C- or better, and meeting the minimum eligibility index (GPA). For transfer applicants, requirements include completion of 60 transferable semester units, a minimum GPA of 2.0 or higher in all transferable college coursework, and completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better.
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of the nature and structure of language. It is concerned with the commonalities of all languages as well as with the ways in which specific languages differ. It is an extremely broad field with many areas of specialization. The Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the core areas of linguistics (phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics) as well as the opportunity to explore various sub-fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in General Linguistics
Requirements: To complete the Bachelor of Arts in General Linguistics or the Bachelor of Arts in Option in Translation Studies, students must fulfill the language requirement by completing a fourth-semester level of a single foreign language (or its equivalent) with a grade of C or better.
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. It seeks to answer questions about the nature of language, how it is acquired, how it is used, and how it changes over time. Linguists study the structure of languages (phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics), the social and cultural contexts of language use (sociolinguistics, anthropological linguistics), the psychological aspects of language (psycholinguistics, language acquisition), and the history of languages (historical linguistics).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics, Option in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) is based on the general undergraduate admission criteria for California State University, Long Beach. Freshmen applicants must be high school graduates, have completed the 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects with a grade of C or better, and meet the required eligibility index (though SAT/ACT scores are currently suspended for admission decisions). Transfer applicants must have completed 60 transferable semester units, have a minimum GPA of 2.0 or higher in all transferable college coursework, be in good standing at the last college or university attended, and have completed the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better.
Concentration: Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
Description: The Option in TESOL is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in teaching English to speakers of other languages. It provides students with a solid foundation in the structure of the English language and the principles of second language acquisition and teaching. The curriculum includes courses in linguistics, language pedagogy, and practical teaching experience. The program is designed for students who are interested in teaching English abroad or in adult education programs in the United States. This degree option is not a K-12 teaching credential program.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Linguistics
Requirements: To declare the minor, students must have completed at least one LING course with a 'C' or better and have a minimum 2.0 GPA.
Description: The minor in linguistics is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the nature of language and the methods of linguistic analysis. It is an excellent complement to majors in foreign languages, English, anthropology, psychology, speech-language pathology, and other fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: To be eligible for undergraduate admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy at CSULB, applicants must meet the general university requirements: high school graduation, completion of the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of 'C' or better, and a qualifying Eligibility Index (GPA). CSULB is a 'test-free' campus and does not use SAT or ACT scores in the admission process for first-year students.
Description: Our undergraduate program is designed to provide students with a broad and solid foundation in the history of philosophy, as well as in the core areas of contemporary philosophy, such as ethics, metaphysics, epistemology, and logic. Students develop critical thinking and communication skills that are valuable in any career path. The philosophy major will: 1. Reasoning Skills: Demonstrate the ability to think critically, including the ability to: identify the thesis of a text, reconstruct the arguments offered in its support, and evaluate those arguments. 2. Communication Skills: Demonstrate the ability to write and speak clearly and effectively, including the ability to: state a thesis, engage in systematic argumentation in its support, and anticipate and respond to objections. 3. History of Philosophy: Demonstrate a basic knowledge of the history of Western philosophy, including the ability to: identify some of the major figures and describe some of the central problems in Ancient, Modern, and 19th and/or 20th Century philosophy. 4. Moral and Political Philosophy: Demonstrate a basic knowledge of moral and political philosophy, including the ability to: identify and describe some of the major figures, theories, and problems in these areas. 5. Metaphysics and Epistemology: Demonstrate a basic knowledge of metaphysics and epistemology, including the ability to: identify and describe some of the major figures, theories, and problems in these areas.

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy
Requirements: This minor is available to any student who has a major in another department. The minor consists of 18 units of philosophy, including: 1. PHIL 100 - Introduction to Philosophy (3 units) or PHIL 101 - Meaning and Value (3 units); 2. PHIL 170 - Critical Reasoning (3 units); 3. 12 units of upper-division philosophy courses.
Description: The Minor in Philosophy is designed for students who want to complement their major with a background in philosophy. It is especially useful for students in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences, and for those who plan to enter professional schools such as law or medicine.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: To graduate with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, students must complete a core of three lower-division courses (POSC 100, POSC 105, and POSC 199) and 33 units of upper-division courses, for a total of 42 units in the major. Political science majors are required to complete POSC 100, POSC 105, and POSC 199 with a grade of "C" or better. Within the major, students choose one of three concentrations: Standard Major; Global Politics; or Law, Politics, and Policy. In addition, students must fulfill the University’s Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR).
Description: The Political Science major is designed for students who want to understand the nature of politics and government and the role of the citizen in the political process. The program provides a broad foundation in the five main subfields of the discipline: American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, and public law. Students learn about the institutions and processes of government in the United States and other countries, the history of political thought, and the principles and practices of international relations. The program also emphasizes the development of critical thinking, research, and writing skills.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Law Politics and Policy
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Law, Politics, and Policy requires a minimum of 36 units for the major. Core Requirements (12 units) include: POSC 100 (Government and Politics in the United States), POSC 311 (Research Methods in Political Science), POSC 391 or POSC 347, and POSC 417 (Legal System and Public Policy). Elective Requirements (24 units) include 9 units from Law and Politics, 9 units from Policy, and 6 units from Public/Private Perspectives. At least one course must meet the Internship or Research requirement (POSC 491, 496, or 498). All courses for the major must be taken for a letter grade. For transfer students, the program requires completion of POSC 100 with a grade of C or better.
Description: The B.A. in Law, Politics, and Policy is designed for students who want to study the way law and politics intersect and the role this intersection plays in the formation of public policy. This interdisciplinary major provides students with a solid foundation in the study of law and policy by drawing on courses from several different disciplines. It is an excellent choice for students who want to go to law school, pursue a career in public policy, or work for a non-profit organization.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Politics
Description: The Department of Political Science and International Relations offers three majors: Political Science, International Relations, and Global Politics. The Global Politics major is designed for students who want to study how countries and other international actors interact with each other, but who want to do so from a more sociological and cultural perspective than is offered in the International Relations major. It is especially suitable for students who want to focus their studies on a particular region of the world. It provides students with a strong foundation in political science and is excellent preparation for a wide variety of careers in government, law, business, and non-profit organizations, as well as for graduate study in political science and related fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Political Science
Requirements: A minor in political science consists of a minimum of 18 units of political science, of which at least 9 units must be upper division. Requirements include: 1. Take one of the following: POSC 100 - Introduction to American Government (3 units), POSC 199 - Introduction to California Government (3 units), or POSC 391 - American Government (3 units). 2. Take 6 units of lower division courses. 3. Take 9 units of upper division courses. The minor is available to any non-Political Science major and requires a minimum GPA of 2.0 for declaration.
Description: This minor is designed for students who want a better understanding of political institutions and processes, but do not have the time to complete the major. Students take one of the introductory courses and then a series of upper-division courses.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Requirements: To be admitted to the psychology major, students must have completed General Psychology (PSY 100) or its equivalent with a grade of 'C' or better. For freshmen, admission is based on the completion of the 'a-g' college preparatory subjects and high school GPA. For transfer applicants, requirements include a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, a minimum GPA of 2.5, and completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning).
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. The goals of the psychology department are to provide students with a comprehensive education in the methods and content of psychology and to prepare students for graduate study or for careers in a variety of fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Psychology
Requirements: To be eligible to declare the minor, students must have completed PSY 100 with a grade of 'C' or better and have at least a 2.0 cumulative GPA. Students must also have completed at least 30 units of college-level coursework. The minor in Psychology requires a minimum of 18 units in psychology, including PSY 100, PSY 110, and PSY 220. At least 9 units must be upper division Psychology courses, and 9 units must be taken in residence at CSULB.
Description: The Minor in Psychology is designed for students who want to obtain some knowledge of psychology but do not want to major in it. It may be especially useful for students majoring in other social sciences, the life sciences, business, or the health professions. A Minor in Psychology is available to any student who is not a Psychology major. The Minor in Psychology consists of a minimum of 18 units of psychology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to CSULB as a first-time freshman, you must: Have completed each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory curriculum (A-G) with a grade of C or better by the end of the spring term prior to fall enrollment. Be a high school graduate or have a GED. Meet the Multi-Factor Admission Criteria. CSULB is impacted at the freshman level and receives more applications than there are spaces available.
Description: The Department of Religious Studies offers students an opportunity to learn about the various religious traditions of the world, including their history, beliefs, practices, and influence on culture and society. Religious Studies is a multidisciplinary field, utilizing various methods of inquiry, including history, sociology, philosophy, psychology, literary criticism, and art history. The major in Religious Studies provides a solid foundation for graduate study in the field of religion, as well as for various careers in education, law, social work, business, and public service. The B.A. in Religious Studies provides students with a broad foundation in the study of religion, while allowing for specialization in particular traditions or themes.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Religious Studies
Requirements: To declare a minor, students must first complete a minimum of 24 units of college coursework with a minimum GPA of 2.0. They should then contact the Religious Studies advisor for more information and to fill out the appropriate paperwork. The Minor in Religious Studies consists of 18 units, including: RELS 100 or RELS 110 or RELS 160; RELS 200 or RELS 202 or RELS 210 or RELS 230; and 12 additional units in Religious Studies, 9 of which must be upper division.
Description: The minor in Religious Studies consists of a minimum of 18 units of religious studies courses, including at least 9 upper division units. The student’s program is developed in consultation with the department’s undergraduate advisor. Courses are chosen to ensure both breadth and depth in the study of religion.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Requirements: Sociology is an impacted major. To be admitted to the Sociology major, students must have completed the following major preparation courses with a grade of 'C' or better: SOC 100 (Introduction to Sociology), SOC 142 (Social Problems), and one of the following: SOC 170, STAT 108, PSY 110, or HDEV 190 (Elementary Statistics). Transfer students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 and have completed 60 transferable semester units. Freshmen must meet the CSU eligibility requirements, including high school graduation and completion of the A-G subject requirements.
Description: The Sociology major provides a scientific understanding of social groups and human behavior. The program focuses on how people interact in groups, how social groups are formed and maintained, and how they affect the behavior of individuals. Students learn to use various theoretical perspectives and research methods to examine the structure of groups, organizations, and societies. Sociology is an excellent major for students who are interested in social change, social justice, and understanding the complex social issues facing our world today.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Sociology
Requirements: To be eligible to declare the minor in Sociology, students must have completed SOC 100 or SOC 142 with a grade of 'C' or better and have a minimum GPA of 2.0. The minor requires a minimum of 18 units in sociology, including: SOC 100 or SOC 142; SOC 335; SOC 356 or SOC 357; and three additional upper-division sociology courses (excluding SOC 495 and SOC 499). A minimum of 9 units in the minor must be taken in residence at CSULB.
Description: The Sociology minor is intended to provide students with a background in the basic concepts and methods of sociology. Sociology is the study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociologists investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies, and how people interact within these contexts. Since all human behavior is social, the subject matter of sociology ranges from the intimate family to the hostile mob; from organized crime to religious cults; from the divisions of race, gender and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture; and from the sociology of work to the sociology of sports. In fact, few fields have such broad scope and relevance for research, theory, and application of knowledge.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish
Requirements: A minimum of 120 units is required. G.P.A. of 2.0 or higher in the major, in all upper division courses, and in overall CSULB units. A grade of 'C' or better is required in all courses counted toward the major. Spanish proficiency at the SPAN 201B level is required for all courses except SPAN 200.
Description: The Spanish degree provides the foundation for students to communicate in Spanish and to have a better understanding of the cultures and literature of the Spanish-speaking world. This major can prepare students for a wide variety of careers in education, business, translation/interpreting, social services, and many other fields. Students in this program will learn to: develop proficiency in Spanish (listening, speaking, reading, writing); critically analyze and discuss literature, film, and other cultural products of the Spanish-speaking world; demonstrate knowledge of the linguistic systems of the Spanish language; and understand the historical, social, and cultural contexts of the Spanish-speaking world.

ProgramName: Minor in Spanish
Requirements: This minor is available to any student. To be eligible for the Spanish Minor, students must have completed SPAN 201B or equivalent with a grade of 'C' or better. All students must see a Spanish Advisor to have the minor officially recorded. Completion of the minor requires 18-20 units. A minimum of 6 upper division units must be taken in residence at CSULB. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in the minor.
Description: This minor is designed to provide students with a good background in Spanish language and Hispanic literature and culture.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Women's, Gender and Sexuality Studies major, transfer applicants must demonstrate a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 and completion of WGSS 101 (Gender, Race, Sex and the Body) or WGSS 102 (Gender, Race, Sex and Society) with a grade of 'C' or better. First-time freshmen must meet the general university admission criteria, which include high school graduation and completion of the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory subjects.
Description: Women’s, Gender and Sexuality Studies is an interdisciplinary field that examines the lives and experiences of women and the social construction of gender and sexuality. Our curriculum provides students with the tools to analyze how gender and sexuality intersect with race, class, ethnicity, nationality, and ability to shape human experience. Students will develop critical thinking, writing, and research skills through a curriculum that emphasizes social justice, community engagement, and global perspectives.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
Requirements: To be eligible to declare the minor in Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies, students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 and have completed at least one WGSS course with a grade of 'C' or better. The minor in Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies is available to any student with a major in another field. A student’s minor program must be approved by the Department Chair or Undergraduate Advisor.
Description: The Department of Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) at CSULB is an interdisciplinary department that places the lives and experiences of women and gender at the center of inquiry. Our curriculum investigates how gender and sexuality intersect with other categories of identity and experience, such as race, class, ethnicity, and nation. We emphasize the development of critical thinking, writing, and research skills and foster a commitment to social justice and community engagement.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Criminology and Criminal Justice
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Criminology and Criminal Justice major, students must meet the following minimum requirements: Complete the following prerequisite courses with a grade of 'C' or better: CRJU 101 (Introduction to Criminal Justice), CRJU 110 (Introduction to Justice Research Methods), SOC 100 (Principles of Sociology), and either POSC 100 (Introduction to American Government) or PSY 100 (General Psychology). Additionally, students must meet the minimum cumulative GPA required for the major. As an impacted program, admission is competitive and based on available capacity.
Department: School of Criminology, Criminal Justice and Emergency Management
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Criminology and Criminal Justice (BSCCJ) program at CSULB is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the study of crime, law, and justice. Our curriculum covers various aspects of the criminal justice system, including policing, courts, corrections, and criminological theory. Students gain a deep understanding of the social, political, and economic factors that influence crime and justice policy. The BSCCJ program prepares students for a variety of careers in the criminal justice field, as well as for further study in graduate or law school.

ProgramName: Minor in Criminology and Criminal Justice
Requirements: Admission to the minor is based on a student’s cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher. To declare a minor in Criminology and Criminal Justice, students must meet with a CCJ advisor and have completed at least 30 units of college coursework. The minor in Criminology and Criminal Justice is available to any non-Criminology and Criminal Justice major. A minimum of 21 units in Criminology and Criminal Justice are required. To complete the minor, students must complete: CRJU 101: The Criminal Justice System (3 units) and 18 additional units of Criminology and Criminal Justice coursework (6 units must be upper-division). All coursework must be completed with a grade of 'C' or better.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The minor is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a career in the criminal justice system or a related field, and who wish to enhance their major field of study with a concentration in Criminology and Criminal Justice. This minor is not available to Criminology and Criminal Justice majors.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Family and Consumer Sciences
Requirements: To be eligible for CSU admission, you must meet the following minimum requirements: High school graduation or equivalent, completion of the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C- or better by high school graduation, and meet the minimum GPA requirement. CSULB uses a Multi-Factor Admission (MFA) process to evaluate applicants.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Concentration: Child Development and Family Studies, Consumer Affairs, Fashion Merchandising and Design, Food Science, and Nutrition and Dietetics
Description: The mission of the Department of Family and Consumer Sciences is to prepare students to be professionals in an ever-changing global society by focusing on the interactions among people and their environments to improve the quality of life for individuals, families, and communities. Students learn to improve the quality of life for individuals, families, and communities through specialized instruction for professional careers and general education in several areas of the department.
Accredidation: The Department of Family and Consumer Sciences is accredited by the American Association of Family and Consumer Sciences (AAFCS).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Child Development and Family Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Child Development and Family Studies major, transfer applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and have completed the following courses (or their equivalent) with a grade of 'C' or better: CDFS 111 or HDEV 180, and one of the following: ANTH 120, BISC 153, BISC 200, BISC 205, BISC 207, BISC 208, or BISC 211. Freshmen must meet general CSU admission requirements, including the completion of the 'a-g' high school subject requirements.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Concentration: Child Development and Family Studies Option; Family Life Education Option
Description: The Child Development and Family Studies (CDFS) program focuses on the study of the family and the development of the individual throughout the life span. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary for working with children, youth, and families in a variety of settings. The program is committed to a diverse student body and prepares students for professional careers and graduate study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Department of Family and Consumer Sciences is accredited by the American Association of Family and Consumer Sciences (AAFCS). The Family Life Education option is approved by the National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for the Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Consumer Affairs
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Consumer Affairs is based on the University’s general admission requirements. Freshmen applicants must graduate from high school, complete the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory study with a grade of C or better, and meet the CSU eligibility index. Transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units with a minimum GPA of 2.0 and have completed the 'Golden Four' General Education courses (Oral Communication, Written Communication, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or better.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Consumer Affairs program provides a general perspective on the field. Students take courses in consumer behavior, consumer laws and issues, consumer protection, personal finance, and management. Careers in consumer affairs include positions in consumer advocacy, consumer communications, and financial services in both the public and private sectors.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Department of Family and Consumer Sciences is accredited by the American Association of Family and Consumer Sciences (AAFCS).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Family Life Education
Requirements: California State University, Long Beach is an impacted campus at the undergraduate level. Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Family Life Education is based on the applicant's ability to meet the eligibility requirements for the major, including a minimum GPA and completion of General Education requirements. The program focuses on the study of families and relationships, preparing students for careers in human service agencies, child care centers, and community organizations.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Family Life Education option is designed for students who are interested in working with families in a variety of settings. The program focuses on the development of individuals and families across the lifespan, and the role of family in society. Students will learn how to design, implement, and evaluate family life education programs, and will gain practical experience through a supervised internship.
Accredidation: The Family Life Education option is an approved program for the Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) credential through the National Council on Family Relations (NCFR).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Fashion Merchandising
Requirements: Admission as a freshman to the program is based on the university's general admission requirements. For transfer students, admission is based on completion of major preparation courses and meeting the required GPA. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5. Required lower-division preparation includes courses in fashion industry, textiles, and fashion merchandising. Students must also complete the General Education requirements as specified by the university.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Fashion Merchandising degree prepares students for careers in the fashion industry. The program provides a strong foundation for students to develop the skills needed for career opportunities in the varied areas of the fashion industry including buying, product development, styling, visual merchandising, and retail management. Students learn about the production, distribution, and consumption of fashion products within a global context.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Department of Family and Consumer Sciences is accredited by the American Association of Family and Consumer Sciences (AAFCS).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Food Science
Requirements: The Food Science program is a Bachelor of Science (BS) degree program that involves the study of the physical, biological, and chemical makeup of food; the causes of food deterioration; and the concepts underlying food processing. Food scientists may develop ways to process, preserve, package, and/or store food, according to industry and government specifications and regulations. The curriculum includes classes in food chemistry, food microbiology, food analysis, food safety, and food engineering.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: Food science is a multi-disciplinary field involving chemistry, biochemistry, nutrition, microbiology and engineering to give one the scientific knowledge to solve real problems associated with the many facets of the food system. The basis of the discipline is the knowledge of the chemistry of food components, such as proteins, carbohydrates, fats and water and the reactions they undergo during processing and storage. A complete understanding of all our food ingredients and how they are processed and packaged is given to students. Specific objects of the program include: Preparing students for careers in the food industry, Educating students for careers in government or other agencies, and Preparing students for graduate study in food science and related fields.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Food Science program at CSULB is one of only a few IFT (Institute of Food Technologists) approved programs in California.

ProgramName: Minor in Family and Consumer Sciences
Requirements: The minor in Family and Consumer Sciences is available to any CSULB student except those who are majoring in any of the options in Family and Consumer Sciences. A student must have a 2.5 GPA or higher in order to declare the minor. To be eligible for the minor, a student must have completed 30 units of college-level coursework. Requirements for the minor: A minimum of 18 units in Family and Consumer Sciences, of which 9 units must be upper-division. All courses must be selected in consultation with a Family and Consumer Sciences advisor.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The minor in Family and Consumer Sciences is designed to provide the student with a broad overview of the various areas of study within the field of Family and Consumer Sciences. It is particularly useful for students in related fields who want to understand the impact of the environment on individuals and families. The minor provides students with the opportunity to explore courses in child development and family studies, consumer affairs, fashion merchandising and design, food science, hospitality management, and nutrition and dietetics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Care Administration
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Health Care Administration major, students must complete the following prerequisite courses with a grade of 'C' or better: ACCT 201, BIOL 207, BIOL 208, ECON 100 or ECON 101, HCA 300, PSY 100, SOC 100, and a qualifying statistics course (STAT 108, STAT 118, HDEV 190, PSY 110, or SOC 170). A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 is required.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Health Care Administration (BSHCA) provides a professional education for students wishing to enter the health care management field in a variety of public and private health care organizations. The BSHCA program is designed to prepare students for management and leadership positions in various health care settings, such as hospitals, health systems, clinics, long-term care facilities, and government agencies. The program’s curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in the core competencies of health care administration, including health care finance, law and ethics, human resources, and strategic management.
Accredidation: The CSULB Bachelor of Science in Health Care Administration program is an undergraduate program certified by the Association of University Programs in Health Administration (AUPHA).

ProgramName: Minor in Health Care Administration
Requirements: To be eligible for the minor, students must have a minimum GPA of 2.5. The Minor in Health Care Administration requires a minimum of 15 units. Requirements include: HCA 300 - The Health Care System (3 units), HCA 312 - Health Care Policy (3 units), HCA 410 - Health Management and Organization (3 units), and 6 units from the following: HCA 341, HCA 353, HCA 402, HCA 416, HCA 417, HCA 422, HCA 428, HCA 450, HCA 457, HCA 465, HCA 468, HCA 480, HCA 481.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The minor in Health Care Administration is designed for students in other majors who want to develop a basic understanding of the healthcare industry and the administration of healthcare organizations. The minor provides an overview of the healthcare system, health law, and health management.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Science
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the major, applicants must demonstrate the following prior to the semester of entry: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0; Completion of the following courses with a grade of 'C' or better: BIOL 207, BIOL 208, CHEM 140 (or 111A), PSY 100, and STAT 108 (or HDEV 190 or PSY 110 or SOC 170). Freshmen: A first-time freshman must meet the University admission requirements. Transfer Students: Upper-division transfer students (60 or more transferable semester units) must meet the University admission requirements.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Concentration: Option in Community Health Education, Option in School Health Education
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Public Health is designed to prepare students for professional practice in public health and related fields, and to provide a foundation for graduate study in public health or other health-related fields. The degree is based on the philosophy of the World Health Organization: 'Health is a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.' Public health is the science and art of preventing disease, prolonging life, and promoting health through the organized efforts and informed choices of society, organizations, public and private, communities and individuals. (Winslow, 1920). Public health professionals work to protect and improve the health of individuals, families, and communities, and to promote health equity by addressing the social determinants of health and reducing health disparities.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Community Health Education
Requirements: To be admitted to the major, students must meet the following criteria: completion of the following courses or their equivalents with a grade of 'C' or better: BIOL 207 (Human Physiology), BIOL 208 (Human Anatomy), CHEM 140 (General Chemistry), PSY 100 (General Psychology) or SOC 100 (Principles of Sociology), and HSC 210 (Personal Health). Applicants must also have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.50 and meet the general University transfer or freshman admission requirements.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Health Science, Option in Community Health Education prepares students for positions as health educators in public, private and voluntary health agencies. This option provides a foundation for students who wish to pursue a Master of Public Health degree. Graduates are eligible to take the Certified Health Education Specialist (CHES®) examination.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The degree programs (BS in Health Science and Master of Public Health) are fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in School Health Education
Requirements: The Option in School Health Education provides students with the required subject matter competency to enter a single subject credential program in health science. In addition to the General Education requirements, the Option in School Health Education requires students to complete 65 units in the major (20 units in the core and 45 units in the option). For admission to the major, transfer students and students changing their major must meet major-specific requirements, which include a minimum GPA of 2.5 and completion of the following prerequisite courses with a grade of 'C' or better: Human Physiology (BIOL 207), Human Anatomy (BIOL 208), and General Psychology (PSY 100).
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: This option is for students who want to become health teachers in middle and high schools. Coursework is aligned with the Single Subject Matter competency requirements for the state of California and prepares students for the Health Science Single Subject Credential program.
Accredidation: Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH)

ProgramName: Minor in Health Science
Requirements: Required courses (9 units): HSC 401, HSC 421, HSC 430. Electives (6 units): Upper division Health Science courses.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The minor in Health Science provides an overview of the public health field and its role in improving health at the population level. Students can choose from a variety of courses that cover topics like health behavior, environmental health, and global health.
Accredidation: The Department of Health Science at CSULB is proud to be accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management, students must meet the general requirements for admission to the university. A minimum GPA of 2.5 is required for the B.S. in Hospitality Management. Transfer students must complete specific lower-division major requirements and have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Hospitality Management program (HM) at CSULB offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) degree. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to be successful in the hospitality industry. The curriculum focuses on the integration of theory and practice through a variety of courses in food service management, lodging management, and tourism and event management. Students are also required to complete a minimum of 800 hours of professional work experience and an internship in the hospitality industry.
Accredidation: The Hospitality Management program at California State University, Long Beach is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Programs in Hospitality Administration (ACPHA).

ProgramName: Minor in Hospitality Management
Requirements: To be eligible for the minor in Hospitality Management, students must have a 2.5 GPA or better in their current major. Students must complete 21 units as specified below with a grade of "C" or better in each course.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The minor in Hospitality Management is available to any non-HM major. The program provides an overview of the industry and focuses on the core areas of hospitality management including food service, lodging, and event planning.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Hospitality Management program at CSULB is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Programs in Hospitality Administration (ACPHA).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the major, applicants must demonstrate the following prior to the semester of entry: Minimum Cumulative GPA: 2.5; Minimum lower division preparation (grade of 'C' or better required): BIOL 207 Human Physiology, BIOL 208 Human Anatomy, KIN 201 Introduction to Kinesiology, PSY 100 General Psychology.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Option in Fitness is designed for students interested in careers in the fitness industry, e.g., corporate wellness, fitness instruction, and personal training. It provides students with a strong foundation in the science of kinesiology and its application to fitness. Students will learn to assess physical fitness, design and implement exercise programs, and motivate individuals to adopt healthy lifestyles.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Exercise Science
Requirements: To be eligible for the Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology, option in Exercise Science, a student must be in good academic standing and have a minimum GPA of 2.5. The student must also complete the following lower-division courses with a grade of 'C' or better: BIOL 207, BIOL 208, CHEM 111A, KIN 201, PSY 100.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology, Option in Exercise Science provides students with the academic and practical experience needed to understand the scientific aspects of physical activity, as well as the practical skills to work with diverse populations. Students learn how physical activity, exercise, and diet influence the function of the human body and the role they play in health and disease. Students find employment as wellness/fitness professionals in clinical settings, community organizations, and private clubs. Students are also prepared for graduate school in any of the exercise science disciplines (biomechanics, exercise physiology, motor control/learning, etc.) or allied health fields (physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician assistant, etc.).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Fitness
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the major, transfer applicants must demonstrate a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and complete the following lower-division preparation courses with a grade of 'C' or better: BIOL 207 (Human Physiology), BIOL 208 (Human Anatomy), and PSY 100 (General Psychology). First-time freshmen must meet the general CSU admission requirements, which include high school graduation and the completion of the 'a-g' college preparatory subject sequence with a qualifying eligibility index.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Option in Fitness is designed for students interested in careers in the fitness industry. The program provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to work as fitness professionals in various settings, including commercial, corporate, and community fitness centers. Graduates of the program are prepared to pursue certifications from organizations such as the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) and the National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA).
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physical Education Teacher Education
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) option, applicants must demonstrate the following: 1. Completion of a minimum of 60 semester units. 2. Minimum cumulative GPA: 2.50. 3. Completion of the following courses with a grade of 'C' or better: ANAT 201 or BIOL 208; PSY 100; and KIN 201. First-time freshmen are admitted to the major as Pre-Kinesiology students and must complete specific lower-division requirements to transition into the PETE option.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Concentration: Option in Physical Education Teacher Education
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology, Option in Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) is a subject matter preparation program in physical education for students who are interested in pursuing a career as a physical education teacher in the K-12 school system. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge, skills, and experiences necessary to become effective physical educators who can promote physical activity and healthy lifestyles in diverse populations. This option is designed for students interested in a teaching career in physical education at the K-12 level. It is a California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC) approved subject matter program. Completion of the program will meet the subject matter requirement for the Single Subject Teaching Credential in Physical Education.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC) approved subject matter program

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sport Psychology and Leadership
Requirements: This is an impacted major. Please refer to the CSULB Admissions website for transfer student and freshman requirements. Minimum grade of 'C' is required in all specific Kinesiology courses and all GE courses used to satisfy the major. Required lower division courses include: PSY 100 (General Psychology), BIOL 207 (Human Physiology), BIOL 208 (Human Anatomy), KIN 201 (Introduction to Kinesiology), and KIN 263 (Techniques of Physical Fitness).
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Sport Psychology and Leadership option provides students with the knowledge and skills to understand the psychological factors that influence performance and physical activity, as well as the leadership and management principles necessary for success in sport-related careers.

ProgramName: Minor in Kinesiology
Requirements: The minor in Kinesiology is available to any student not majoring in Kinesiology. To be eligible for the minor in Kinesiology, a student must have: 1. A GPA of 2.5 or higher in the following courses: BIOL 207, BIOL 208, and PSY 100. 2. A minimum of 21 units (at least 9 units must be upper division) to include: BIOL 207 - Human Physiology (4 units), BIOL 208 - Human Anatomy (4 units), KIN 201 - Introduction to Kinesiology (3 units), PSY 100 - General Psychology (3 units). And 9 additional units of Kinesiology courses (at least 6 upper-division). Each course must be completed with a grade of “C” or better. To declare the minor, students must have completed all the prerequisite courses.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The minor in Kinesiology is available to any non-Kinesiology major. The minor consists of a minimum of 21 units. Six (6) of these units must be upper-division. Students must complete all courses with a grade of 'C' or better. No more than 3 units of activity courses (KIN 100-198) can be used towards the minor. Note: All upper-division courses must be taken in residence at CSULB.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nursing
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) at CSULB, applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in: 1. All prerequisite courses, 2. Overall college GPA, and 3. Science prerequisite GPA (Human Anatomy, Human Physiology, Microbiology, and General Chemistry). Prerequisites include BIOL 207 (Human Physiology), BIOL 208 (Human Anatomy), BIOL 201 (Microbiology), CHEM 140 (General Chemistry), Written Communication, Oral Communication, Critical Thinking, and Statistics. Additionally, applicants must complete the Test of Essential Academic Skills (TEAS) exam (Version 7) with a minimum score of 58.7%. Admission is highly competitive and is based on a scoring rubic that factors in GPAs and TEAS scores.
Description: The School of Nursing (SON) at California State University, Long Beach is a premier provider of nursing education. SON is known for its high standards and excellence in its BSN and MSN programs. We are dedicated to providing students with the skills and knowledge needed to be successful in their careers as nurses. The Basic Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program is designed for students who are beginning their initial nursing education. This program prepares students for the Registered Nursing licensure examination (NCLEX-RN) and for a career in professional nursing.
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing and master's degree program in nursing at California State University, Long Beach are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org). The baccalaureate degree program in nursing is also approved by the California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition and Dietetics
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Nutrition and Dietetics, applicants must meet the general CSULB admission requirements. For Freshmen, this includes completion of the 15-unit 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C or better and graduation from high school. For Transfer students, admission is based on the completion of major-specific lower-division prerequisites including General Chemistry (CHEM 111A or 140), Organic Chemistry (CHEM 227), Human Physiology (BIOL 207), and Microbiology (BIOL 201) with a minimum GPA (usually 2.5 or higher depending on impaction). The program is impacted, meaning additional criteria or a higher GPA may be required for admission.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nutrition and Dietetics provides students with a strong foundation in the physical and biological sciences, as well as a comprehensive understanding of the role of nutrition in health and disease. This program is designed for students interested in careers as Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDN), nutritionists, or health professionals in various settings, including hospitals, community health agencies, food industries, and private practice.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) at California State University, Long Beach is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Recreation
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Recreation, transfer applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 and have completed PSY 100 with a grade of 'C' or better. Freshman applicants must be high school graduates and meet the CSU requirements for the 'A-G' college preparatory sequence with a grade of 'C-' or better. Standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) are not used for admission purposes.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Concentration: Community Recreation, Parks and Outdoor Recreation, Recreation Therapy, Tourism Management
Description: The Recreation Administration Bachelor of Arts degree provides students with a high-quality education and prepares them for a wide range of professional opportunities in the recreation, parks, and tourism field.
Accredidation: The Recreation Administration program is accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Parks, Recreation, Tourism and Related Professions (COAPRT).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Recreation Therapy
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science in Recreation Therapy is an impacted major. To be considered for admission to the major, applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and have completed all General Education (GE) Foundations (A1: Oral Communication, A2: Written Communication, A3: Critical Thinking, and B4: Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of 'C' or better.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: Recreation therapy (RT) is the use of recreation and other activities as a form of treatment to improve the physical, emotional, social, and cognitive health of people with disabilities or illnesses. Recreation therapists work with people of all ages in a variety of settings, including hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, and community centers. They design and implement programs that help people to: Improve their physical health and fitness, Develop their social skills, Manage their emotions, Increase their independence, Improve their quality of life. The Recreation Therapy program at Long Beach State is designed to prepare students for a career as a recreation therapist. Students in the program take courses in a variety of topics, including: Human anatomy and physiology, Psychology, Recreation therapy theory and practice, Program planning and implementation, Assessment and evaluation. The program prepares students to become a Certified Therapeutic Recreation Specialist (CTRS) through the National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification (NCTRC) and a California Board of Recreation and Leisure Certification (CBRC).
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Parks, Recreation, Tourism and Related Professions (COAPRT).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social Work
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Social Work (BASW) program, applicants must meet the following criteria: a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5; completion of the following prerequisite courses with a grade of 'C' or better: SW 220 (Introduction to Social Work), PSY 100 (General Psychology), SOC 100 (Introduction to Sociology), and an approved General Education Statistics course. In addition to applying to the university, applicants must submit a supplemental application to the School of Social Work, which includes a personal statement and a resume.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Social Work (BASW) is a professional program that prepares students for entry-level, generalist social work practice. The curriculum provides students with the knowledge, values, and skills necessary for practice with individuals, families, groups, organizations and communities. The program is designed to help students develop the ability to think critically, use scientific inquiry to inform practice, and to advocate for social and economic justice. Students are prepared to work with diverse populations in a variety of settings.
Accredidation: The BASW program is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE).
CostPerCredit: $420 per unit for non-residents in addition to mandatory fees

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Speech-Language Pathology
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the major, applicants must demonstrate the following at the time of application: Completion of a minimum of 60 transferable semester units; Completion of the entire General Education (GE) Breadth requirements; A minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.0 or better; Completion of the following prerequisite courses or their equivalents with a grade of 'C' or better: PSY 100 (General Psychology), STAT 108 or PSY 110 (Statistics), BIOL 200 or BIOL 201 or BIOL 205 or BIOL 207 (General Biology), and PHYS 100 or CHEM 100 or CHEM 111A (Physical Science).
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The undergraduate program (B.A.) in Speech-Language Pathology provides students with basic information about the development and processes of speech, language, and hearing; and the diagnosis and treatment of communication disorders. It is designed to prepare students for graduate study in speech-language pathology and/or audiology. The curriculum includes courses on the anatomy and physiology of the speech and hearing mechanisms, phonetics, language development, and various communication disorders. Completion of the B.A. degree does not qualify a student to practice as a speech-language pathologist or audiologist.

ProgramName: Minor in Speech-Language Pathology
Requirements: The minor in Speech-Language Pathology is available to any student who has completed at least 30 units of college coursework and has a minimum GPA of 3.0. Prior to being allowed to declare the minor, students must meet with a Department of Speech-Language Pathology advisor.
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description: The minor in Speech-Language Pathology provides students with an introduction to the fields of speech-language pathology and audiology. It provides foundational information on the nature of communication and its disorders across the lifespan.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
