ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in General Biology
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Biology is competitive as it is an impacted major. Freshmen applicants are evaluated based on their high school GPA in 'a-g' courses. Transfer applicants must have completed 60 transferable units, including General Education requirements and major-specific prerequisites: General Biology I & II (BIOL 211 & 212), General Chemistry I & II (CHEM 111A & 111B), and Survey of Calculus or Calculus I (MATH 119A or 122), all with a grade of 'C' or better and a minimum required cumulative GPA.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Biology is a highly structured program designed for students who are interested in a career in the biological sciences. The program provides a broad background in the biological sciences and allows students to specialize in one of several areas of interest. All students who wish to earn a B.S. degree in Biology must select one of the following options: Biology Education, Botany, Marine Biology, Microbiology, Molecular Cell Biology and Physiology, or Organismal Biology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marine Biology
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Marine Biology, applicants must meet the general CSU admissions requirements and major-specific criteria. This major is impacted. Freshman applicants are evaluated based on their GPA and completion of the A-G subject requirements. Transfer applicants must have completed a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, maintained a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5, and completed the following lower-division preparation courses with a grade of 'C' or better: General Biology (BIOL 211 and BIOL 212), General Chemistry (CHEM 111A and CHEM 111B), and Calculus I (MATH 122).
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Marine Biology program at CSULB is one of the largest and most distinguished programs of its kind in the United States. We offer a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in Marine Biology. Students in our program take a suite of core courses in biology, chemistry, physics and math, and then choose from a wide variety of upper-division courses to tailor their degree to their specific interests. These upper-division courses cover topics ranging from the biology of marine organisms (e.g. marine mammals, fish, sea turtles, invertebrates, algae) to the ecology of marine ecosystems (e.g. kelp forests, coral reefs, wetlands, the open ocean) to the application of modern techniques in marine science (e.g. molecular ecology, GIS, physiological ecology, oceanography).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the major, applicants must demonstrate the following: Minimum cumulative GPA: 2.5; Minimum grade of “C” in the following: MATH 119A or MATH 122, CHEM 111A, CHEM 111B, BIOL 211, BIOL 212, BIOL 213.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Microbiology is designed to provide students with a broad education in the biology of microorganisms. The program includes courses in microbial physiology, genetics, and diversity, as well as several elective courses that allow students to focus on specific areas of interest, such as medical microbiology, immunology, or environmental microbiology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular Cell Biology and Physiology
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Molecular Cell Biology and Physiology is based on competitive criteria. First-time freshmen must complete the 'A-G' college preparatory sequence with a minimum GPA. For transfer applicants, the program requires a minimum cumulative GPA (typically 2.5 or higher) and completion of major-specific prerequisites with a grade of 'C' or better, including General Chemistry (CHEM 111A or equivalent), General Biology (BIOL 211 and 212 or equivalent), and Calculus (MATH 119A or 122 or equivalent).
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Molecular Cell Biology and Physiology provides a strong foundation in the processes that occur within and among cells and the function of those cells in the context of the whole organism. This program is designed for students interested in careers in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and other health professions, as well as those pursuing graduate studies or careers in biotechnology, research, and academia.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Zoology
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Biology, Option in Zoology, first-time freshman applicants must meet the following minimum requirements: High school graduation, completion of the 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory curriculum with grades of C or better, and a minimum GPA. For transfer students, admission is based on the completion of major-specific requirements including General Biology, General Chemistry, and Calculus with a minimum grade of C.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Botany
Requirements: To be considered for admission as a freshman, you must: graduate from high school or equivalent, complete the 15-unit comprehensive 'a-g' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C- or better, and meet the Multi-Factor Admission Score (MFAS) criteria. For transfer students, requirements include: completion of a minimum of 60 transferable semester units, a minimum GPA of 2.0 or higher in all transferable college coursework, and completion of the 'Golden Four' General Education requirements with a grade of C- or better. Specific major-specific requirements for the Botany option include completion of BIOL 211, BIOL 212, CHEM 111A, and MATH 119A or MATH 122 with a grade of 'C' or better.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: This degree is designed for students seeking a broad background in the biological sciences and who are particularly interested in the study of plants. Students are provided with a strong foundation in the basic principles of biology, with an emphasis on plant diversity, structure, function, and ecology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Ecology
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science in Biology, Option in Ecology, Evolution, and Marine Biology focuses on the study of organisms and their environments. To be admitted to the major, students must meet major-specific requirements, including the completion of specific lower-division courses such as General Biology (BIOL 211 & BIOL 212), General Chemistry (CHEM 111A), and Calculus (MATH 119A or MATH 122) with a grade of 'C' or better.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The B.S. in Biology, Option in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology is intended for students who have an interest in ecology, evolutionary biology, and the diversity of life. The curriculum is broad and provides a solid foundation for students who want to explore careers in biological research, ecology, evolutionary biology, or conservation biology, or who plan to continue their education in graduate school.

ProgramName: Minor in Biology
Requirements: To earn a minor in biology, a student must have a minimum of 15 units of upper-division biology courses. All courses used to satisfy the requirements for the minor must be passed with a grade of 'C' or better. At least 9 units of upper-division biology courses must be taken in residence at CSULB. The minor in biology is not available to Marine Biology or Biology majors. Requirements include completion of BIOL 211 (5 units), BIOL 212 (4 units), BIOL 213 (4 units), and CHEM 111A or CHEM 111B (5 units), plus 15 units of upper-division biology courses (at least one must include a laboratory).
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Biology minor is designed to provide students with a broad background in the biological sciences. It is available to students in any major except for those in the Department of Biological Sciences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry program at CSULB is based on general university undergraduate admission criteria and major-specific requirements. Freshmen must meet the Multi-Factor Admission Criteria, which includes completion of the 15-unit 'a-g' college preparatory course pattern and high school GPA. For transfer students, eligibility is determined by the completion of 60 transferable semester units, the 'Golden Four' general education requirements, a minimum GPA of 2.5, and the completion of specific major-preparatory courses including General Chemistry I and II (CHEM 111A and 111B), Calculus I (MATH 122), and General Physics (PHYS 151 or 100A) with a grade of C or better.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Chemistry degree is for students who want a background in chemistry as a basis for higher study in other areas such as business, law, or medicine, or for those who plan to teach at the secondary level. It is not intended for students who want to become professional chemists.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to CSULB as a freshman, you must: Have graduated from high school, have earned a Certificate of General Education Development (GED) or have passed the California High School Proficiency Examination (CHSPE); Have completed with a grade of C or better each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory subjects (A-G); Have a minimum 'a-g' GPA; and Meet the Major Specific Requirements for the major you are applying to. For Bachelor of Science in Chemistry, freshmen applicants must meet a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and a minimum GPA of 2.5 in Mathematics and Science courses.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry is designed to provide a broad-based education in chemistry that is appropriate for students planning to continue their education in graduate school or to find employment in the chemical industry or a related field. The B.S. Chemistry program at CSULB is certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS).
Accredidation: The B.S. Chemistry program at CSULB is certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS).

ProgramName: Minor in Chemistry
Requirements: This minor is available to any student who is not a Biochemistry or Chemistry major. Take all of the following: CHEM 111A - General Chemistry (5 units), CHEM 111B - General Chemistry (5 units), CHEM 251 - Quantitative Analysis (4 units), CHEM 371A - Organic Chemistry (3 units), CHEM 371B - Organic Chemistry (3 units). Take one of the following: CHEM 441A - Biological Chemistry (3 units) or CHEM 451 - Instrumental Methods of Analysis (5 units).
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry offers a Minor in Chemistry. To be eligible for a Minor in Chemistry, students must complete a minimum of 24 units in chemistry of which at least 15 must be upper division. All upper division courses must be taken in residence at CSULB.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth Science
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Earth Science is based on both general CSU eligibility and major-specific requirements. Freshmen applicants must meet the 'A-G' college preparatory requirements with a grade of C or better and are evaluated using a STEM Index that considers high school GPA and math GPA. For transfer students, the program requires a minimum GPA of 2.5 and the completion of specific major preparation courses, including Calculus I (MATH 122), General Chemistry (CHEM 111A), Physical Geology (GEOL 102 and 104, or GEOL 106), and Physics (PHYS 151 or PHYS 100A) with a C or better.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Earth Science is designed for students who are interested in Earth Science as a career but who do not intend to become professional geologists. It provides a broad background in Earth Science and is particularly appropriate for students who are interested in a career in secondary education. Students who want to become professional geologists should follow the B.S. in Geology program.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Earth Science
Requirements: This minor is designed to provide a broad introduction to the Earth sciences. It is available to all students regardless of major. Contact the undergraduate advisor in Geological Sciences for further information. Completion of a minimum of 18-21 units is required.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: This minor is available to any student not majoring in Geological Sciences. It is particularly appropriate for students in other science or engineering majors, or for those intending to teach science in middle or high school.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geology
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Geology, applicants must meet the general CSU undergraduate admission requirements. For first-time freshmen, CSULB uses a multi-factor admission process that considers the applicant's high school GPA and other factors. For transfer students, admission is based on the completion of major-specific requirements including specific lower-division courses such as General Chemistry (CHEM 111A), Calculus (MATH 122), Physics (PHYS 151), and Geology (GEOL 102 and 104, or 106) with a minimum grade of C or better. All applicants must meet the minimum CSU eligibility and the major-specific criteria for the College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Geology is designed for students who intend to pursue a career in geology or who wish to continue their studies at the graduate level. It provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences and mathematics and a broad, rigorous background in the geological sciences. The B.S. in Geology is the primary degree for students seeking to become licensed professional geologists.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Minor in Geology
Requirements: This minor is available to any student who has completed the lower-division requirements for a major in the physical or biological sciences or engineering. To earn a minor in Geology, a student must complete a minimum of 18 units in geological sciences, of which at least 12 units must be upper division. All Geology courses taken for the minor must be completed with a grade of 'C' or better.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: This minor is designed for students with other majors who wish to obtain a background in geology. The curriculum is flexible to allow students to emphasize either a more traditional or an environmental geology track.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Data Science
Requirements: To be considered for admission as a first-year student, applicants must have graduated from high school, have completed with a grade of 'C' or better the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory 'a-g' subjects, and meet the minimum Eligibility Index. California State University has suspended SAT and ACT requirements for undergraduate admission decisions.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Applied Data Science (BSADS) is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to manage, analyze, and interpret data in a variety of contexts. This program is offered by the College of Engineering in collaboration with the College of Liberal Arts and the College of Health and Human Services. The program includes concentrations in Health Informatics, Social Science, and Business Analytics, allowing students to apply their data science skills to a specific field of interest.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics program at CSULB is competitive. For freshmen, eligibility is determined by a multi-factor admission process that considers high school GPA and completion of 'a-g' courses. The CSU has suspended the use of ACT/SAT scores for admission. For transfer students, requirements include a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and the completion of the following major-specific prerequisites with a grade of 'C' or better: MATH 122 (Calculus I), MATH 123 (Calculus II), MATH 224 (Calculus III), and MATH 247 (Linear Algebra).
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematics is intended for students who are interested in pursuing a graduate degree in mathematics or who want to pursue a career in a mathematical field in industry or government.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics is based on both general university requirements and major-specific criteria. Transfer applicants must complete the following major preparation courses with a grade of 'C' or better: MATH 122 (Calculus I), MATH 123 (Calculus II), and MATH 224 (Calculus III). Freshmen applicants must meet the general CSU admission requirements, which include high school graduation, completion of the 'A-G' college preparatory sequence, and meeting the minimum GPA requirements. The major is part of an impacted college, and admission may be more competitive.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics program is designed for students who want to apply math to other fields. It includes a strong background in mathematical and computational techniques, and offers students the flexibility to choose a variety of courses in their area of interest. This program is suitable for students who want to pursue a career in industry or government, or who want to pursue graduate studies in applied mathematics or a related field.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Statistics
Requirements: To be considered for freshman admission to CSULB, you must: Complete each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory curriculum (A-G) with a grade of 'C' or better by the end of the spring term prior to fall enrollment; and Graduate from high school by the end of the spring term prior to fall enrollment. Admission to CSULB is competitive and the university is impacted for all undergraduate majors, meaning CSULB uses supplemental criteria to determine admission. For graduate admission, applicants must hold an acceptable baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution, be in good academic standing at the last college or university attended, and have attained a grade point average of at least 2.50.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Statistics is designed to provide students with the necessary tools to perform data analysis, use statistical software, and apply statistical methodology to solve problems in various fields. The program prepares students for careers in industry, government, or for further graduate study in statistics or related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics Education
Requirements: To be admitted to this option, a student must have a minimum GPA of 2.5 and must have completed MATH 122 with a grade of 'C' or better. A student must complete at least 120 units. A grade of C or better must be achieved in each of the following lower-division courses: MATH 122 - Calculus I (4 units), MATH 123 - Calculus II (4 units), MATH 224 - Calculus III (4 units), and MATH 247 - Introduction to Linear Algebra (3 units).
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: This option is intended for students who wish to become secondary school mathematics teachers. It is a program of subject matter preparation in mathematics that has been approved by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC). Students who complete the program are not required to take the CSET (California Subject Examinations for Teachers) for the purpose of demonstrating subject matter competency for a single subject credential in mathematics.
Accredidation: Approved by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC)

ProgramName: Minor in Mathematics
Requirements: This minor is available to any student not majoring in Mathematics. Requirements include: MATH 122 - Calculus I (4 units), MATH 123 - Calculus II (4 units), MATH 224 - Calculus III (4 units), and MATH 247 - Introduction to Linear Algebra (3 units). In addition, a minimum of 9 units of upper-division mathematics courses (excluding MATH 303, MATH 309, MATH 370A, MATH 370B, and MATH 409) is required. These 9 units must be chosen in consultation with a Department of Mathematics and Statistics undergraduate advisor. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in the minor.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: This minor is available to any student who has a major in another field. A minor in mathematics is a good choice for any student who is majoring in a science, engineering, or another field where math is used, and it is also a good choice for students who simply enjoy mathematics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Requirements: To be admitted to the Physics, B.S. program, students must meet general university admission requirements. Freshmen are admitted based on the CSU eligibility index. For transfer students, admission is based on completion of major-specific preparation courses including Calculus I (MATH 122), Calculus II (MATH 123), Calculus III (MATH 224), and General Physics I (PHYS 151) and General Physics II (PHYS 152) with a grade of C or better. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and a minimum GPA of 2.5 in all required math and science courses is required.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: Physics is the study of the physical world, from the smallest subatomic particles to the largest structures in the universe. It is the most fundamental of the sciences and provides the foundation for all other sciences and engineering. The Bachelor of Science in Physics is intended to provide a solid foundation for those who wish to pursue careers in physics or related fields, or who plan to attend graduate school in physics or a related field.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
CostPerCredit: $420/unit (non-resident fee in addition to basic tuition)

ProgramName: Minor in Physics
Requirements: To earn a minor in physics, a student must complete a minimum of 24 units in physics, including: PHYS 151 - Mechanics and Heat (4 units), PHYS 152 - Electricity and Magnetism (4 units), PHYS 254 - Applied Modern Physics (3 units), PHYS 255 - Laboratory in Modern Physics (1 unit). In addition, at least 9 units of upper-division physics courses must be completed (excluding PHYS 390, PHYS 491, PHYS 495 and PHYS 496). PHYS 310, PHYS 320, PHYS 340, PHYS 350, PHYS 380 are recommended upper-division courses. PHYS 490 and PHYS 492A may be used with the consent of the Department. A GPA of at least 2.0 must be maintained in the courses required for the minor.
Department: College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Description: The minor in physics is available to any student who has a major in another field. It provides a solid foundation in the principles of physics and their applications.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Art is based on the university's general undergraduate admission criteria. Freshmen applicants must complete the 15-unit comprehensive 'A-G' pattern of college preparatory courses with a grade of C or better and meet the Eligibility Index (a combination of GPA and high school coursework). The BA in Art program does not require a portfolio or supplemental application materials for admission.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Art is a liberal arts degree with two options: Art History and Studio Art. This degree provides a broad education in the visual arts, emphasizing a strong foundation in art history, theory, and practice. It is designed for students who want a well-rounded education in the arts while also having the flexibility to explore other academic interests.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art Education
Requirements: First-time freshman applicants must have graduated from high school, completed the 'a-g' college preparatory subjects with a grade of C or better, and meet the CSULB Index which considers the applicant's 'a-g' GPA. All School of Art prospective students are first admitted as 'Pre-Art' majors. After completing specific lower-division requirements and maintaining a minimum GPA, students may apply to enter the BA in Art, Option in Art Education.
Department: College of the Arts, School of Art
Description: The Art Education program at CSULB is a community of artist-educators who are committed to social justice, community engagement, and the development of the artistic voice in all students. Our program prepares students for careers as art teachers in K-12 schools, as well as in museums, community centers, and other educational settings. Our curriculum is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in studio art and art history, as well as the pedagogical skills and knowledge necessary to be effective art educators in the 21st century. The B.A. in Art Education is a pre-professional degree that provides students with the subject matter preparation required to enter a Single Subject Credential Program in Art.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Art History is a 120-unit program. Students are required to take 12 units of lower-division Art History courses, 30 units of upper-division Art History courses, and 3 units of a Studio Art course. Additionally, Art History majors must demonstrate proficiency in a foreign language at the intermediate level. The foreign language requirement can be met by taking a placement exam or through coursework (usually 4 semesters or 12-16 units). Applicants to the BA in Art History do not require a portfolio for admission and should follow the general University requirements and deadlines for admission via Cal State Apply.
Description: The Art History program at California State University, Long Beach provides students with a broad knowledge of the history of art and visual culture. Students learn to analyze works of art from a variety of perspectives, including historical, social, and cultural contexts. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research, and writing skills, preparing students for careers in museums, galleries, non-profit organizations, and for graduate study in art history or related fields.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Studio Art
Requirements: Prospective students must first apply to the University during the CSU initial application filing period (October 1 – November 30 for the following Fall semester) through Cal State Apply. Upon admission to the university, all Studio Art students are entered as BA in Studio Art majors. Students applying to the BA in Studio Art do not submit a portfolio. Current CSULB students (those who have completed at least one semester at CSULB) may apply to the Studio Art major if they meet the eligibility requirements.
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) is a professional degree that provides students with more in-depth study in their chosen studio area. Most BFA students will focus on one of the following areas: Ceramics, Drawing & Painting, Fiber, Illustration, Photography, Printmaking, or Sculpture/4D. Students who are interested in the BFA should apply for the BA in Art and then apply to the BFA program after completing their foundation art courses and several courses in their area of focus.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art
Requirements: Acceptance into the BFA in Art, Option in Illustration is based on a portfolio review. Open to students who have completed all lower division requirements in Art and who have a minimum GPA of 3.0 in Art and a minimum GPA of 2.5 in their overall college work. Portfolio submission is mandatory and must be submitted via SlideRoom during specific application windows (October for Spring admission, March for Fall admission).
Description: Students in the Illustration track are prepared to create imagery for a variety of media, including: Books, Graphic novels, Magazines, Newspapers, Advertising, Comic books, Corporate communications, Product packaging, and Video games. Students can specialize in specific areas of the field through their elective choices, which include courses in: Traditional and Digital Media, Character Design, Storyboarding, Editorial Illustration, 3D Modeling, Illustration for Children’s Books, Creative Writing, Animation, and Printmaking. The curriculum focuses on developing a student’s personal vision through both conceptual and technical skills. In addition to regular coursework, the Illustration area hosts guest lecturers and workshops by industry professionals and provides opportunities for student interaction with the illustration community through field trips and participation in the student illustration club.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Ceramics
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Ceramics is by portfolio review. Applicants must submit an artist statement (no more than 500 words) and a portfolio of 10-15 images of recent work. Prospective students must also meet the general undergraduate admission requirements for California State University, Long Beach, which include the completion of lower-division art prerequisites for current or transfer students.
Description: The Ceramics Program provides a supportive, yet challenging environment that prepares students for professional careers as artists and educators. Through a rigorous curriculum, students are encouraged to explore the breadth of the medium from utilitarian pottery and design to sculpture, installation, and public art. The curriculum focuses on building technical expertise through specialized courses in glaze chemistry, kiln technology, and varied forming processes, while challenging students to find their unique creative voices and to understand their practice within the framework of historical and contemporary art and design. Our facilities are among the largest and most complete in the world, with over 15,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor studio space, including 25 kilns. This unique environment allows students to work on a large scale, utilize specialized firing techniques, and gain experience in professional kiln maintenance and construction. The proximity of several dedicated ceramic art galleries and museums, as well as a vibrant professional community, provides students with a wealth of opportunities for engagement and professional development.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Drawing and Painting
Requirements: To be eligible to apply for the BFA in Drawing and Painting, students must be enrolled in or have completed ART 291. Admission to the BFA is by portfolio review only. Requirements include the completion of lower-division courses: ART 130, ART 131, ART 181, ART 184, ART 121, ART 150, ART 230, ART 251A or 251B, and ART 291. The application process requires a portfolio of 10-15 images and a 300-500 word Statement of Purpose describing the student's art practice, goals, and reasons for applying to the BFA program.
Description: The BFA in Drawing and Painting prepares students for a career in the fine arts and for graduate study. This intensive program is intended for students who want to develop their own personal vision through a rigorous practice of traditional and contemporary drawing and painting. At the center of the program is the development of a student’s independent studio practice. Students engage with a variety of technical and conceptual approaches, including observational and representational methods, abstraction, and the expanded field of painting. The program provides students with a broad knowledge of historical and contemporary art through art history courses and seminars, as well as regular critiques and discussions with faculty and peers. Graduates of the program are prepared to enter the professional art world as artists, educators, and gallery professionals.
Accredidation: All programs in the School of Art are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Graphic Design
Requirements: Admission into the Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Graphic Design is a two-step process. Students must first be admitted to the university as Art majors. To be eligible for the BFA portfolio review, students must have completed or be in the process of completing the following lower-division art foundation courses: ART 110 (Introduction to the Visual Arts), ART 130 (Foundation Two-Dimensional Design), ART 131 (Foundation Three-Dimensional Design), and ART 181 (Foundation Drawing). The BFA is a professional degree that requires a competitive portfolio review for entry into the upper-division program.
Department: College of the Arts, School of Art
Description: The B.F.A. in Art with an Option in Graphic Design is a professional degree that focuses on intensive work in graphic design supported by a program of general studies. The program prepares students for careers in the field of graphic design and provides a foundation for graduate study.
Accredidation: Accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Illustration/Animation
Requirements: Admission into the BFA in Illustration/Animation is by portfolio review. Students must first be admitted to the University as a Pre-Art major. To be eligible to apply for the BFA, students must have completed Art lower division core and program specific prerequisites (such as ART 130, 131, 181, and 184). For BFA eligibility, students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in their Art and Art History courses. Applicants must submit a portfolio of work via SlideRoom, which must include a 500-word Artist Statement.
Department: College of the Arts, School of Art
Description: The Illustration and Animation tracks at CSULB School of Art provide a solid foundation in the techniques and concepts of both traditional and digital media. Our curriculum is designed to prepare students for professional careers in the animation and illustration industries, including film, television, games, and publishing. The program emphasizes professional standards, creative exploration, and technical proficiency, helping students develop a personal artistic voice while gaining the skills necessary for the entertainment and publishing industries.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Photography
Requirements: The BFA is a professional degree that requires students to complete a supplemental application. To be eligible for admission to the BFA in Photography, you must: 1. Be admitted to CSULB as an Art major. 2. Complete the following program prerequisites with a grade of 'C' or better: ART 131, ART 181, ART 184, ART 281. 3. Have a minimum 3.0 GPA in program prerequisites. 4. Submit a portfolio and an artist statement for review by the photography faculty.
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts is a professional degree that provides students with a thorough grounding in fundamental principles and techniques, and prepares them for professional practice as artists or for graduate study. The Photography program provides students with a wide range of aesthetic and technical experiences in the field of photography. Students are encouraged to develop their own individual practice through the exploration of traditional and digital technologies, as well as history and theory.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Printmaking
Requirements: Current students at CSULB who wish to apply to the BFA in Printmaking program must complete a portfolio review for admission. The portfolio review for the BFA in Printmaking takes place once a year in the spring semester. New transfer students who wish to apply to the BFA in Printmaking program must first apply to the university as an Art major during the initial CSULB application period. Once accepted to the university, students may apply to the BFA program by participating in the Printmaking portfolio review. Application Requirements: 1. Unofficial transcripts from all colleges attended (including CSULB). 2. Artist Statement (no more than 500 words). 3. 10 - 15 images of work (at least 5 images must be printmaking work).
Description: The BFA in Printmaking is a professional degree that prepares students for a career as a professional artist, a master printer, or for graduate-level study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in 3-D Media
Requirements: Admission to the BFA in 3-D Media is a two-step process. Students must first be admitted to the university as Art majors. To enter the BFA program, students must complete lower-division foundation courses (including ART 130, 131, 150, 181, and 184) and maintain a minimum 3.0 GPA in all art and art history courses. Applicants must then pass a BFA Portfolio Review, which requires the submission of 10-15 images of original work and an artist statement via SlideRoom.
Concentration: Ceramics, Fiber, Metal and Jewelry, Wood
Description: 3-D Media is a multi-disciplinary program that focuses on the study of materials, craft, and art. The program offers tracks in Ceramics, Fiber, Metal and Jewelry, and Wood. Students are encouraged to develop their own creative voices through the exploration of traditional and contemporary processes, techniques, and concepts. The curriculum emphasizes technical proficiency, aesthetic development, and critical thinking. Students have access to well-equipped facilities and are supported by a faculty of active artists and scholars. The program prepares students for careers as studio artists, designers, and educators, as well as for further study at the graduate level.
Accredidation: The School of Art at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Minor in Art
Requirements: A minor in Art History is available to any CSULB student. 21 units are required. 12 units must be unique to the minor. 12 units must be upper-division. 6 upper-division units must be taken in residence. Required courses include: AH 111A - Foundation Art History: Prehistory-Medieval (3 units), AH 111B - Foundation Art History: Renaissance-Contemporary (3 units), and 15 units of upper-division Art History courses (AH 300-499).
Description: The Minor in Art History is available to any student. Completion of the minor will provide students with a foundational knowledge of art history and the ability to analyze art and visual culture within its historical context.
Accredidation: The School of Art at CSULB is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Dance
Requirements: Admission to the Department of Dance is by audition. New students must first apply to the university via Cal State Apply (www.calstate.edu/apply) between Oct. 1 and Nov. 30. A separate Department of Dance audition application is also required and can be found on the CSULB Dance website. All applicants must be admitted to the university before they can be officially admitted to the major. Admission to the Department of Dance is for Fall semester only.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Dance is a liberal arts degree providing students with a broad-based education in dance, while allowing them the flexibility to pursue other areas of interest. This degree is designed for students who want a strong foundation in dance and who may be interested in dance-related careers such as dance education, dance science, or arts management.
Accredidation: The Department of Dance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance
Requirements: Admission into the BFA in Dance is by audition only. To be eligible to audition for the BFA program, a student must be a current CSULB dance major, have completed one year of the BA program, and be in good academic standing. Transfer students must complete one semester of the BA program at CSULB before auditioning for the BFA. Students must have: At least a 3.0 GPA in all Dance courses; Completed DANC 120 and DANC 150. The audition for the BFA consists of technique classes (modern and ballet), the performance of a solo (2-minute maximum), and an interview. Additionally, applicants will be asked to complete a short writing prompt on the day of the audition.
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) degree in Dance is a 132-unit professional degree that prepares students for careers as performers and/or choreographers. The BFA program focuses on intensive training in contemporary and ballet technique, alongside courses in choreography, dance science, dance history, production, and music for dance. Performance and choreographic opportunities are central to the BFA experience, culminating in a senior project. Admission to the BFA program is by audition only.
Accredidation: The Department of Dance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Dance Science
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Dance Science program is contingent upon two main factors: 1. Acceptance to the University as a Dance major during the CSU application period. 2. Successful completion of the Departmental Placement Audition. All prospective students, including freshmen and transfers, must audition for the Department of Dance for placement. The audition typically includes technique classes in ballet and modern dance. Applicants must also meet general California State University (CSU) undergraduate admission criteria.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Dance Science provides a program of study that combines dance with specific science courses for students interested in a career in dance medicine and science, and/or interested in pursuing graduate work in related fields such as physical therapy, dance science, dance medicine, or other health and wellness fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Department of Dance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD).

ProgramName: Minor in Dance
Requirements: This minor is available to any student who meets the prerequisites for the required courses and has the approval of the Dance Department. To be eligible for the Dance Minor, a student must be a current CSULB student and have a minimum GPA of 2.0. To declare the minor, students must meet with the Dance Department advisor. A minor in Dance requires a minimum of 23-25 units. All students (majors and minors) are required to take a technique placement exam to enroll in any level of modern or ballet higher than 101.
Description: The Minor in Dance is available to any student in the University who can meet the technical requirements for upper division classes. Audition or placement into technique levels is required.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Department of Dance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Design
Requirements: Admission to the B.S. in Industrial Design is a two-step process. First, students are admitted to the University as Pre-Industrial Design majors. Second, students apply for the B.S. in Industrial Design after completing specific lower-division requirements including DESN 120A, DESN 120B, DESN 132A, DESN 132B, DESN 141, DESN 142, DESN 143, DESN 150, DESN 232, and DESN 246. Formal admission into the major is based on a mandatory portfolio review of student work. The program is impacted, and applicants must meet the minimum GPA and prerequisite requirements specified by the Department of Design.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Interior Design
Requirements: Admission into the BFA in Interior Design is a two-step process. First, students are admitted to the University as Pre-Design majors. Second, students must participate in a portfolio review to be admitted into the BFA in Interior Design. This review typically occurs after the completion of specific lower-division core courses (including DESN 120A, 120B, 132A, 132B, 141, 142, 143, 150, 151, 154, 156, and 232). A minimum 2.5 GPA is required for CSULB students to enter the Pre-Design major.
Description: The BFA in Interior Design is a professional degree that focuses on the design of interior environments. This program is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA) and the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD). Our program prepares students for professional practice through a curriculum that emphasizes design process, technical skills, and the health, safety, and welfare of the public.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA) and the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Electronic Arts
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Film and Electronic Arts is an impacted major. Admission is based on the university's general admission requirements for impacted majors. The program offers two options: Theory and Practice of Cinema, and Narrative Production. Admission to the Narrative Production option is highly competitive and requires a supplemental application including an artist statement, a digital portfolio, and a writing sample (short story or script). Transfer applicants must complete specific lower-division preparation courses, including FEA 205 and FEA 299, with a grade of 'C' or better to be eligible for admission.
Concentration: Narrative Production; Theory and Practice of Cinema
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Film and Electronic Arts is designed to give students a comprehensive overview of the field, with a choice of two options: Narrative Production or Theory and Practice of Cinema. The Department of Film and Electronic Arts provides a professional-level film/video and electronic media education within a liberal arts context. Its goal is to create filmmakers, video/digital artists and scholars who have a knowledge of the history, theory and techniques of their chosen media and an awareness of the ways in which those media function in our society.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Minor in Film and Electronic Arts
Requirements: Admission to the minor is by permission of the Department. To be eligible for the minor, students must have completed FEA 205 with a grade of 'C' or better and have a minimum GPA of 2.5. Students must meet with the FEA academic advisor to declare the minor.
Description: The Minor in Film and Electronic Arts is designed for students who want to explore the history, theory and production of film and electronic media. It is an excellent choice for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of the media and how it is created, while also pursuing another major. The minor provides students with a foundational understanding of film and electronic media through a combination of history, theory, and production courses. This minor is available to any non-FEA major who has completed FEA 205 with a grade of 'C' or better. This minor is not available to FEA majors.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Department of Film & Electronic Arts is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Arts in Music, students must first meet the university-wide admission requirements for California State University, Long Beach and then pass an audition on their primary instrument or voice. Additionally, applicants must submit a supplemental application through the Bob Cole Conservatory of Music via Acceptd, which includes a one-page musical resume and a repertoire list.
Department: Bob Cole Conservatory of Music, College of the Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music is a liberal arts degree. It is designed for students who wish to pursue a broad-based education in music while also having the flexibility to take a significant number of courses in other disciplines. This degree is often chosen by students who are interested in double-majoring or who wish to prepare for a variety of careers in or outside of music.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bob Cole Conservatory of Music, applicants must: 1. Complete the University Application (Cal State Apply). 2. Complete the Conservatory Supplemental Application (SlideRoom). 3. Successfully complete an audition or interview for their specific instrument or area of study. First-time freshmen must have a minimum 3.0 overall high school GPA. Transfer students must have a minimum 2.0 overall college GPA.
Department: College of the Arts, Bob Cole Conservatory of Music
Concentration: Composition, Music History and Literature, Instrumental Performance, Jazz Studies, Piano Performance, Vocal Performance
Description: The Bachelor of Music is a professional degree in music with concentrations in performance, music history and literature, and composition. The curriculum is designed to provide a high level of specialized training for students who intend to pursue professional careers in music. In addition to general education requirements, students must complete music core requirements and requirements for one of the concentrations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Composition
Requirements: All Composition applicants must submit a portfolio containing 3-4 original scores of varying instrumentation and recordings of the pieces (if available). Applicants are also required to submit a musical resume and a statement of purpose through the supplemental application. Furthermore, applicants must pass a Theory Placement Exam, complete an interview with the composition faculty, and perform an audition on their primary instrument or voice.
Description: The Composition program at the Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is designed to help students develop their unique creative voices as composers of contemporary concert music. Students in the program receive weekly individual lessons with our composition faculty and participate in a weekly Composition Seminar. The curriculum provides a thorough grounding in the technical aspects of composition, including orchestration, counterpoint, and electronic music, as well as a broad exposure to the music of our time.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Education
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Music in Music Education, applicants must complete the University application via Cal State Apply and the Bob Cole Conservatory of Music supplemental application through SlideRoom. Admission is based on a successful performance audition on a primary instrument or voice. Additionally, all students applying for this specific program must participate in an interview with the Music Education faculty, which includes questions regarding their interest in music education, their musical background, and their teaching experiences.
Department: Bob Cole Conservatory of Music, College of the Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Music, Option in Music Education is a professional degree that prepares students for a career in music education. This program provides students with a broad and thorough foundation in music, including performance, music theory, music history, and conducting, as well as specialized coursework in music pedagogy and professional education. The program is designed to meet the requirements for the California Subject Matter Competency in Music, preparing graduates to enter a credential program to teach music at the elementary and secondary levels. Students in the program must select one of three tracks: Choral, Instrumental, or General Music.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). The Music Education program is also approved by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CTC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Performance
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Music in Performance, applicants must complete a two-step process: 1) Submit a university application through Cal State Apply and 2) Submit a supplemental application to the Bob Cole Conservatory of Music (BCCM) via Acceptd. Admission is based on both academic eligibility for California State University, Long Beach and a successful performance audition. Required supplemental materials for the conservatory application include a musical resume, a personal statement, and letters of recommendation. Specific audition repertoire is required based on the student's primary instrument or voice.
Department: Bob Cole Conservatory of Music, College of the Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Music degree is designed for students who seek professional careers in music performance, composition and music education. The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). Degrees offered are the Bachelor of Music (B.M.) and the Master of Music (M.M.).
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: Accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM)

ProgramName: Minor in Music
Requirements: The Minor in Music is available to any student who has been admitted to the university. Acceptance into the minor requires an audition/interview with the appropriate faculty member. All students must complete a minimum of 18 units in music, of which at least 6 must be upper-division.
Description: The Minor in Music is available to any student who is not a music major. The minor allows the student to continue their musical studies and participate in Conservatory ensembles while pursuing a major in another field. Admission to the Minor in Music is by audition only.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The Bob Cole Conservatory of Music is a fully accredited member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre Arts
Requirements: Admission into the Performance/Acting program is by audition and interview only. Auditions are for students who have been accepted into CSULB through the University Admissions process. For the most current information regarding admission into CSULB as a freshman or transfer student, please check the CSULB Admissions website. Preparation for the Performance/Acting interview/audition: Bring a current photo and a current resume of your theatrical experience. Present two contrasting monologues from published modern or contemporary plays. The audition will consist of the performance of your prepared pieces and an interview with the Performance faculty. Total time: 5 minutes.
Description: The Performance-Acting Option is an intensive pre-professional training program intended for students who have a career in professional theatre as their goal. This program provides the student with an opportunity to integrate the physical, vocal, and emotional aspects of the acting process with the goal of developing a unique, expressive, and technically skilled actor/artist. Students take a series of courses in acting, movement, and voice, as well as courses in theatre history, dramatic literature, and technical theatre. Students are also required to participate in departmental productions, both on stage and behind the scenes.
Accredidation: The Department of Theatre Arts is a member of and accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Minor in Theatre Arts
Requirements: The Minor in Theatre Arts is open to any student at the university. This minor requires a minimum of 18 units, including THEA 101, THEA 111, THEA 114A or 114B, THEA 221 or 222, and 6 units of upper-division theatre electives selected in consultation with the department’s undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of Theatre Arts offers a Minor in Theatre Arts for students majoring in other fields who wish to develop an understanding of the theatre and its history, or to participate in theatre activities. Students must complete a minimum of 21 units, of which 12 must be upper division.
Accredidation: The Department of Theatre Arts at California State University, Long Beach is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accountancy
Requirements: Accountancy is an impacted major at CSULB, meaning it receives more applications than can be accommodated. To be admitted to the major, students must meet specific GPA and prerequisite course requirements. This includes the completion of the following major preparation courses with a grade of 'C' or better: ACCT 201, ACCT 202, ECON 100, ECON 101, and MATH 115 (or MATH 112A and MATH 112B, or MATH 122). Freshmen must also meet general CSU eligibility based on a combination of high school GPA and completion of 'A-G' college preparatory subjects. Transfer students must have completed at least 60 transferable units including the specific major prerequisites.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Accountancy is designed to provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge to succeed in the accounting profession. The program offers a curriculum that is rigorous and demanding, preparing students for the challenges of a career in accounting. The mission of the Department of Accountancy is to provide high-quality accounting education that prepares students for careers in public accounting, private industry, and government/not-for-profit organizations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. The Department of Accountancy also holds separate AACSB accreditation for its accounting programs.

ProgramName: Minor in Accountancy
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have a minimum GPA of 2.5 and have completed ACCT 201 with a grade of 'C' or better. The minor in Accountancy is available to any non-Accountancy major.
Description: The Minor in Accountancy is available to any student who is not a Business major. The program provides a foundational understanding of accounting principles and practices for students pursuing degrees outside of the College of Business.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business). The Department of Accountancy also holds separate AACSB accreditation for its accounting programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Finance
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with an option in Finance is competitive as it is an impacted major. Freshman applicants must meet minimum CSU eligibility requirements, including high school graduation, completion of the 15-unit 'a-g' college preparatory pattern with grades of C- or better, and a qualifying admission index. Transfer applicants must have completed at least 60 transferable semester units, be in good standing at the last institution attended, and have a minimum GPA of 2.50. Specific major-specific requirements for transfers include the completion of the following prerequisite courses with a grade of 'C' or better: ACCT 201 (Elementary Financial Accounting), ACCT 202 (Elementary Managerial Accounting), ECON 100 (Principles of Macroeconomics), ECON 101 (Principles of Microeconomics), MATH 115 or 122 (Calculus for Business or Calculus I), and STAT 108 or 118 (Statistics for Business or Elementary Statistical Analysis).
Description: The Finance Department at CSULB offers an undergraduate program that leads to a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with an Option in Finance. Our program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in financial theory and practice, preparing them for a wide range of careers in the financial services industry. Our curriculum covers a broad range of topics, including corporate finance, investments, financial markets and institutions, and real estate. We also offer a range of elective courses that allow students to specialize in areas such as international finance, derivatives, and financial modeling.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: Accredited by AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business)

ProgramName: Minor in Finance
Requirements: To be eligible to declare the minor in Finance, a student must: 1. Have a minimum CSULB GPA of 2.5. 2. Have completed ACCT 201 and ECON 101 with a grade of “C” or better. To be awarded the minor in Finance, a student must: 1. Have completed the following 15 units with a grade of “C” or better: FIN 300 - Business Finance, FIN 350 - Capital Markets and Institutions, and 9 units of upper division finance electives (FIN 300-499). All courses must be completed with a grade of “C” or better.
Description: The minor in finance is designed for students who want to develop a background in finance to complement their major field of study. This minor is available to all CSULB students (except for Finance majors). To be eligible for the minor in finance, students must have a declared major and have completed at least 30 units with a minimum GPA of 2.5. They must also have completed the following courses with a grade of “C” or better: ACCT 201, ECON 101, and MATH 115 (or MATH 119A or MATH 122).
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International - The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Resources Management
Requirements: To be considered for admission as a freshman, you must: 1. Complete each of the courses in the comprehensive pattern of college preparatory 'a-g' subjects with a grade of C or better by the end of the spring term prior to fall enrollment. 2. Be a high school graduate or have a GED. 3. Meet the minimum CSU eligibility index. As an impacted major, the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with an option in Human Resource Management requires applicants to meet higher GPA and major-specific prerequisite requirements. Transfer applicants must complete specific lower-division core courses including accounting, economics, business law, and mathematics (calculus and statistics) with minimum grade requirements.
Description: Human Resource Management (HRM) is the strategic approach to the effective management of people in a company or organization such that they help their business gain a competitive advantage. It is designed to maximize employee performance in service of an employer's strategic objectives. HRM is primarily concerned with the management of people within organizations, focusing on policies and on systems. HR departments are responsible for overseeing employee-benefits design, employee recruitment, training and development, performance appraisal, and rewarding (e.g., managing pay and benefit systems). HR also concerns itself with organizational change and industrial relations, that is, the balancing of organizational practices with requirements arising from collective bargaining and from governmental laws.
Accredidation: AACSB International

ProgramName: Minor in Human Resources Management
Requirements: To be eligible to declare the Minor in Human Resource Management, a student must have a minimum GPA of 2.5 in all college courses and have completed at least 30 units. The minor is available to all CSULB students except for Human Resource Management majors.
Description: The Human Resources Management Minor is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the theories, policies and practices used by organizations to manage their human resources. The minor is available to all students except those majoring in Business Administration with an option in Human Resources Management.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Information Systems
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Information Systems, applicants must meet the general university admission requirements. For first-time freshmen, this includes completion of the 'a-g' college preparatory subjects with a grade of C or better and meeting the minimum Eligibility Index. For transfer students, applicants must have completed 60 transferable semester units with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.50. Transfer students must also complete the following major-specific prerequisite courses with a grade of 'C' or better: ACCT 201, ACCT 202, ECON 101, ECON 102, MATH 115 (or MATH 112B or MATH 122), and STAT 108.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Information Systems (BSIS) is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in both business and information technology. Students will learn how to design, develop, and manage information systems that support business processes and decision-making. The program also focuses on developing students' analytical and problem-solving skills, as well as their ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The College of Business at CSULB is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Minor in Information Systems
Requirements: To be eligible for the minor in Information Systems, a student must have a minimum GPA of 2.50 in all college and university coursework. Students must also have completed IS 233 with a grade of 'C' or better. To be awarded the minor in Information Systems, a student must complete the following: IS 300, IS 310, IS 340, IS 380, and IS 480. A minimum of 15 units must be taken in residence. All courses must be completed with a grade of 'C' or better.
Description: The minor in Information Systems is available to all students except those majoring in Information Systems. Many organizations need people who understand how to apply information technology to their specific functional areas. This minor is designed to provide students with the opportunity to gain knowledge and skills to effectively use information technology in their chosen careers.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).
Accredidation: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International - The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in International Business
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Science in International Business major, students must meet the following requirements: Completion of the following lower-division courses with a grade of 'C' or better: ACCT 201, ACCT 202, ECON 100, ECON 101, MATH 115 (or higher), and STAT 108. Students must also meet the minimum GPA requirements for the College of Business and be admitted as a Pre-International Business major prior to declaring the major.
Description: The International Business (IB) program at CSULB is a multidisciplinary program that prepares students for the challenges and opportunities of the global business environment. The program provides students with a solid foundation in the core business disciplines, such as accounting, finance, marketing, and management, as well as specialized knowledge in international business topics, such as international trade, international finance, international marketing, and international management. The program also emphasizes the development of cross-cultural communication and negotiation skills, as well as the ability to adapt to different cultural and business environments. Students are required to gain proficiency in a second language and to complete a study abroad or international internship experience.
Accredidation: The College of Business at CSULB is accredited by AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Minor in International Business
Requirements: The Minor in International Business is available to all CSULB students (except for International Business majors) who have a 2.5 GPA or higher. Prerequisites for the minor are: ECON 100 or ECON 101 with a grade of “C” or better; ACCT 201 with a grade of “C” or better. To be eligible to declare the minor, students must have a 2.5 GPA or higher.
Description: The Minor in International Business is designed to provide students with a global perspective on business and to prepare them for careers in the global marketplace. The minor is open to all CSULB students (except for International Business majors) who have a minimum GPA of 2.5.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for California State University, Long Beach is [www.csulb.edu](https://www.csulb.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Management
